stages.label: Braga typical edition approved in December 1924
stages.limitations: These rules describe the 1924 state; their absence from 1558 has not been established. Later inserted feasts in this copy must not be assigned to 1924. The batch-4 inspection does not show which 1924 contents were new in 1924: the 1558 book was not reached, so the Palm blessing agreement with Bragança's 1558 count and the presence of modern feasts are recorded as 1924 contents, not as 1924 changes.
stages.reception: The bull requires this missal for priests of the Archdiocese of Braga. This establishes the contemporary prescription, not universal subsequent observance or present law.
stages.scope: The title edition and its binding approval/conformity rules; no complete body reconstruction. Batch 4 adds directly inspected 1924 body loci: the Palm Sunday blessing, the Sacred Heart and Assumption Masses and the end-of-October sequence.
stages.summary: Approved 8 December and declared typical 9 December 1924. Future Holy See changes to Masses already contained in it must be applied; newly imposed universal feasts must enter the Braga calendar. The 1924 body prints the Palm blessing with five prayers before the preface Qui gloriaris in consilio sanctorum and Haec tibi Domine festa recoluntur after the Sanctus; the Sacred Heart Mass Egredimini with the preface of the Cross; and the Assumption Mass Gaudeamus. Its index of feasts names local feasts such as the consecration of the archdiocese to the Sacred Heart (16 May) and the coronation of the Immaculate of Sameiro (12 June).

stages.label: Braga 1924 altar copy with bound supplements to 1961
stages.limitations: A physical copy's accretion, not a new edition: the supplements are separately approved leaves bound into a 1924 book, and the scan's order reflects binding and uploader assembly. The body pages still print the superseded 1924 formularies. The copy does not prove when any church adopted each supplement, and absence of a later leaf from this copy proves nothing about its issue. Some approbation dates were read from low-resolution images.
stages.reception: The inserts carry their own approbations: Sacred Congregation of Rites concordats, Turin archdiocesan concordats or imprimaturs, and Braga archiepiscopal imprimaturs. Not every leaf carries Braga approval: the Christ the King leaf has only a Turin concordat and imprimatur (7 April 1927) with a Marietti imprint, and the final page of the 1929 Sacred Heart leaf has only the Rites concordat. Binding into this Braga altar copy shows they were supplied for use with it; actual use in a named church is not established.
stages.scope: One digitized altar copy of the 1924 Braga missal into which supplement leaves with their own Rites concordats or Braga imprimaturs were bound; selected propers and the insert sequence only.
stages.summary: Twenty-one inserts supply later Masses for this Braga altar book: the 1929 Sacred Heart Mass Cogitationes with its own preface, Christ the King (Turin 1927), the Assumption Mass Signum magnum (Braga 16 December 1950), the Common of Supreme Pontiffs (1942/1947), the votive Mass of Christ the Eternal High Priest (1935/1936) and saints from Teresa of the Child Jesus (1925/1928) to Gregory Barbarigo and Anthony Mary Claret as third-class feasts (Braga 21 November 1961).

stages.label: Early printed Carthusian missal with a brief Ordinary block before the Canon
stages.limitations: Provisional (cold review 2026-10-22): the year is a catalogue attribution, not read in the book, and the catalogues differ in precision (BSB-Ink [1496]; GW not after 1496); the inspected block shows no textual difference from Pavia 1561 that is encoded as a change. The year is a catalogue attribution, not read in the book. Only the block before the Canon was read; the water prayer, incensation and Orate fratres were not found on canvases 230–234, which bounds a search of this block, not of the whole book. A complementary Ordinarium may have carried such rubrics.
stages.reception: Printed for the Delft bookseller Eckert van Homberch; ownership and use in a named charterhouse are not established.

stages.summary: The patent of Frater Petrus, Prior of the Grande Chartreuse and Minister General, dated at the Grande Chartreuse 28 August 1560 under the General Chapter's authority, licenses the Pavia charterhouse to print the Order's missals and other books in the same form as the editions of Thielman Kerver of Paris (now sold out), the large missals first printed at Lyon being also exhausted, and forbids other printings without licence. The Gloria reads propter gloriam tuam magnam; the water prayer is De latere Domini nostri Iesu Christi; the chalice offering is In spiritu humilitatis; and the Orate asks prayer pro me peccatore.

evidence.claim: Ordinis Cartusiensis: Calendarium proprium (30 nov. 2018; Prot. 156/18).
Approval line: Congregation for Divine Worship, 30 November 2018, Prot. N 156/18.
Lists the distinctive features (a)-(h) of the restored missal.
Names the 1917 Kalendarium perpetuum as the revised base.

stages.label: Postconciliar Carthusian proper calendar confirmed in 2018, printed in the 2021 missal
stages.limitations: The approval date belongs to the calendar, not to the whole missal; the missal's own recognition date and the reported 1981 printing remain unestablished. The 2021 PDF is unofficially hosted.
stages.reception: Approved by the Holy See for the Order; Praenotanda n. 15 adds house calendars, so observance varies by charterhouse.
stages.scope: The Order's proper calendar as confirmed on 30 November 2018 and printed in the 2021 missal; no prayer text. The 2021 Praenotanda are reported as that book's own description, not as part of the 2018 approval.
stages.summary: The Congregation for Divine Worship confirmed the Carthusian proper calendar on 30 November 2018 (Prot. 156/18), and the 2021 missal prints that approval at the head of its calendar. The calendar Prooemium says it revises the Kalendarium perpetuum approved by the Congregation of Rites on 28 February 1917. The 2021 book's Praenotanda n. 2, whose own approval date is unknown, lists the restored missal's distinctive features: more prefaces and formularies taken from the Roman Missal, Communion under both kinds, conventual concelebration, a universal prayer on Sundays and solemnities, an enlarged body of orations, more Commons, revised votive Masses and some vernacular use.

stages.limitations: The 1502 original is mediated by Henderson’s critical reprint. The witness difference does not identify when or why the prayers diverged, nor prove a diocesan decree removing a local feast.
stages.reception: The printed title reports bishop, dean and chapter authority; geographical uptake remains unestablished.
stages.scope: Selected proper differences from the Whitchurch manuscript.
stages.summary: The printed second-Sunday-of-Lent Secret is Ecclesiae tuae, Domine, munera placatus assume. Henderson reports that the manuscript’s Dubricius Mass is absent from the printing.
stages.witness_label: Missale Herfordense, Rouen: Pierre Olivier and Jean Mauditier for Jean Richard, 1502; represented by Henderson 1874

evidence.claim: Lists the early prints and describes their limited differences and continuing shared errors.

stages.label: York’s closely related printed witnesses
stages.limitations: This bounded witness group is not one complete reconstructed book or five independently proved recensions. The first print is undated; c. 1509 is the editor’s attribution. His proposed manuscript ancestry is explicitly tentative.
stages.reception: Printed intended use is York. Henderson describes substantial earlier manuscript ceremonial diversity, so the printed state must not be projected backwards to all medieval York books.
stages.scope: Henderson’s bounded comparison of five printed editions.
stages.summary: The earliest printing lacks the monthly calendar notices and places Modus finiendi Collectas and Considerationes circa Missam differently. Henderson reports shared errors across the sequence, including an omitted Holy Saturday rubric line and Petrocius placed in April rather than June; musical note lengths also vary.
stages.witness_label: York missals: Violette, undated c. 1509; Gachet 1516; Bernard/Cousin 1517; Gachet 1530; Regnault 1533

evidence.claim: Identifies the main volume and dates the witness 1320–1341.
States the earlier repertory and compares it with the fifteenth-century witnesses.

stages.label: Notated missal’s larger medieval repertory
stages.limitations: The manuscript is incomplete and composite surviving material must be mapped carefully. Its fuller repertory may include options rather than mandatory observance of every listed item.
stages.reception: A medieval Esztergom exemplar; no claim that every listed saint or sequence was used in every celebration.
stages.scope: Preparation placement and proper/sequence repertory compared by Déri with 1484.
stages.summary: Déri counts approximately 210 saints with special propers and 78 sequences in the fourteenth-century notated missal. It also includes the Pentecost-octave Mass and the Transfiguration grape blessing that his later comparators lack. Preparation follows the Holy Saturday baptismal order.
stages.witness_label: Missale notatum Strigoniense ante 1341; main volume AM Bratislava EC Lad 3, with related surviving material

evidence.claim: Reproduces the 31 August 1484 colophon, printer and chapter/vicar authority.
Describes preparation placement, sanctoral reduction and sequence comparison.

stages.label: Esztergom’s 1484 printed repertory
stages.limitations: The 1484 book is not identified as the moment when all differences first arose. Déri expressly requires more complex relationships than a single subtraction/addition sequence; the Pálóczi comparator already shares much of the later state. The absent intervening preparation texts could be a copying omission or assumed memorized text, not a proven ritual abolition.
stages.reception: The colophon identifies Esztergom use and the vicar and chapter’s assent; survival of a printing does not demonstrate uniform implementation.
stages.scope: Selected repertory and arrangement changes reported in Déri’s edition.
stages.summary: Compared with the pre-1341 witness, the special-proper sanctoral is reduced by about one third. The later sequentiary retains 39 of the earlier 78 sequences and adds ten others; its material substantially agrees with the intervening Pálóczi manuscript. Preparation prayers move to the beginning of the book.
stages.witness_label: Missale Strigoniense, Nuremberg: Anton Koberger, completed 31 August 1484; Déri’s critical text

stages.date_label: Rome, ad Sanctae Sabinae, 1985; promulgation letter of Master Vincent de Couesnongle dated 15 August 1983; printing mandate of Master Damian Byrne, 3 April 1985 (Prot. 50/85/310)

evidence.claim: CD 671/76 (25 July 1977) allows the Order's peculiar elements ad libitum; CD 1590/77 (18 February 1978) confirms the Latin Proprium Missarum and lectionary texts; CD 998/80 (7 November 1980) confirms the Latin Masses of the Order's Blessed; later grants follow.

The 1968 chapter sought adoption of the restored Roman rite, the Roman Missal and then the new Roman Order of Mass were adopted, and the volume is presented as a supplement to the Roman Missal; note 5 cites CD 98/69 of 2 June 1969.
evidence.locus: Promulgation letter nn. 3–5 and note 5, printed pp. X–XI (PDF 8–9)

evidence.claim: The Congregation's 2 June 1969 concession of the Roman Missal and calendar to the whole Order, with licences for the former rite and interim feast grades.
Confirmation of the chapter decree on the Office and Dirks's account of the 1968 decision to adopt the Roman rite.

stages.label: 1985 Dominican Proprium: Missal and Lectionary as a supplement to the Roman Missal
stages.limitations: Only the front matter and promulgation letter were read; the body is not collated against the 1604 printing or the 1933, 1939 and 1965 Dominican missals, so no transition is drawn from any earlier Dominican stage. The 1969 Roman adoption and interim calendar, the 1971 Office confirmation and the 1983 promulgation are recorded as evidence here, not as separate book states; the stage date is the 1985 publication.
stages.reception: The 1969 concession allowed superiors to license priests to keep the Dominican rite then in force; the date of each house's changeover and any licensed continuation are not evidenced. The 1985 mandate directs vernacular editions to conform to this typical edition; actual use of the Latin volume in named houses is not established.
stages.scope: The Order's postconciliar proper for Mass in one typical volume: ritual elements of the proper of time, the proper of saints, the lectionary of saints and chant indications, for use with the restored Roman Missal. It is not a complete independent Dominican Missal.
stages.summary: The 1968 River Forest chapter decided to adopt the restored Roman rite, and on 2 June 1969 the Order received leave to assume the restored Roman Missal and calendar. Master Vincent de Couesnongle promulgated this Missal and Lectionary of the Order's proper and declared the Latin edition typical by a letter dated 15 August 1983; Master Damian Byrne ordered it printed on 3 April 1985, and it was published in 1985. Its front matter prints the confirmations of the retained peculiar elements (1977), the Latin proper and lectionary texts (1978) and the Masses of the Order's Blessed (1980).
stages.witness_label: Proprium Ordinis Praedicatorum: Missale et Lectionarium, editio typica, Rome 1985 (order-hosted facsimile)

evidence.claim: Lists separate 1774 ordinary, 1775 sacramental ritual and 1775 rites-and-lections titles.
Describes prayer, ritual and calendar additions associated with the first printed Taksa.

The 1960 Roman liturgical commission states that in the Missal edited at Rome in 1774 nothing appears besides the Apostles' anaphora except Epistles and Gospels taken from the Roman Missal and arranged by its calendar.
evidence.locus: Praefatio Commissionis Liturgicae, printed v (PDF 3), second paragraph

stages.label: First Roman printed ordinary and lection collection
stages.limitations: No original 1774/1775 page comparison. The two Eucharistic books are not two successive revisions. The retrospective does not securely assign every item to an individual volume. The 1960 commission's description of the 1774 edition's proper is a retrospective that does not distinguish the 1774 ordinary from the 1775 lessons volume.
stages.reception: Prepared for Malabar Catholic worship; no claim that every reported addition originated in 1774.
stages.scope: Complementary Eucharistic volumes; the sacramental ritual is excluded.
stages.summary: The official retrospective reports received Maronite prayers, Latin-derived vesting and Holy Week material, and altered calendar/readings.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Chaldaicus Missae Beatorum Apostolorum (1774); Ordo Chaldaicus rituum et lectionum (1775)

evidence.claim: Explicitly names Propaganda printings of 1775 and 1845 and describes the earlier arrangement.
Calls the Masses approved on 31 July 1905 newly appended after comparison with the exemplar; only their prior absence is inferred.

stages.label: Propaganda exemplar named as 1845
stages.limitations: Propers scope is limited to the reported absence of the newly appended 1905 Masses, not a complete proper inventory. Documented as a named exemplar, not an independently identified physical edition or a proven substantive revision of 1775. Do not equate it with the separately reported 1844 lection book or 1845 sacramental ritual.
stages.reception: An authorized editorial exemplar for the 1906 Malabar book; its actual historical use is not reconstructed.
stages.scope: Bounded earlier arrangement and absence of the later-approved appended Masses, as described in the 1904/1905 permissions.
stages.summary: The permission describes an exemplar with dispersed ordinary material and Rogation readings in a supplement.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syro-Chaldaeo-Malabaricum, Propaganda printing dated 1845 by the 1904 permission

evidence.claim: Directs collection of the ordinary and relocation of Rogation readings.
Reports comparison with the exemplar and newly appended Masses approved by the Congregation of Rites on 31 July 1905.
evidence.locus: Physical PDF 6, 15 October 1905 approval and 1906 imprint

evidence.claim: The reproduced 10 August 1905 official reply reports the Rites 31 July nulla osta for the requested insertion.
Opening native entries identify Francis Xavier (3 December), Nicholas (6 December), Ambrose (7 December), Holy House (10 December) and Lucy (13 December).

Running heads of PDF 68–23 (printed 56*–101*) read on 2026-10-21: the section is titled throughout as added feasts (ʿeʾdē mawsfē) arranged by month — Kanun I/December 55*–56*, Kanun II/January 57*–58*, Shbat/February 59*–64*, Adar/March 65*–67*, Nisan/April 68*–69*, Iyar/May 70*–71*, a Sacred Heart of our Lord feast 72*, Haziran/June 73*–76*, a second feast headed 'of the Heart' 77*, Tammuz/July 78*–81*, Ab/August 82*–83*, a separately headed feast 84*, Elul/September 85* and 87* with the Holy Name of Mary 86*, Teshri I/October 88*–93*, Teshri II/November 94*–97*, and a separately headed closing block 98*–101*.

stages.label: Reorganized travel missal with appended Masses
stages.limitations: The added section's month-by-month structure and three separately headed feasts are read from running heads; individual entries inside each month block are not enumerated, the headers at 77*, 84* and 98*–101* are not securely read beyond their opening words, and no prayer body is transcribed. The older appendix 1*–54* is not attributed to the 1905 permission.
stages.reception: Aloysius Pareparambil petitioned also on behalf of the other two Syrian apostolic vicars. Propaganda’s reply reports the Rites nulla osta for insertion; the 15 October 1905 imprimatur authorizes printing. Neither record establishes universal actual adoption.
stages.scope: Andreas Kalapura edition: arrangement and additions explicitly described in its permissions.
stages.summary: Collects the ordinary, moves the three pre-Septuagesima Rogation readings into place, and adds the 1905-authorized Masses in a distinct 55*–101* section, beginning with December feasts.
stages.witness_label: Ordo chaldaicus rituum et lectionum, Puttenpalli, Mar Thoma Sliha Press, 1906

evidence.claim: Describes the edition against which Vadakel’s changes are stated.

stages.label: Roman exemplar described by the 1946 editor
stages.limitations: No date or exact Roman printing is named. This contextual state cannot be merged with the 1845 exemplar without further evidence.
stages.reception: Malabar liturgical exemplar, not the Latin Roman Missal; the phrase Roman Edition indicates printing context here.
stages.scope: Only features explicitly contrasted by the 1946 foreword.
stages.summary: Prayers/rubrics were dispersed; some feasts appeared only in the calendar; server prayers were merely indicated; Marian Huthama was absent.
stages.witness_label: Unidentified Roman edition named in Augustine Kandathil’s foreword to Vadakel 1946

evidence.claim: Dates the printing and explicitly describes the changed content and arrangement.
evidence.locus: Physical PDF 2–4, title, foreword and contents

evidence.claim: Names Holy See letter Prot. 2521/28 of 3 September 1930 for double-asterisk feasts and the Immaculate Conception Gospel.

stages.label: Vadakel’s corrected and expanded arrangement
stages.limitations: Bodies of the ordinary, propers and appendix are absent from the excerpt. No direct descent from the 1906 book is asserted. The 1930 act is reported in the book, not independently inspected.
stages.reception: Approved by Augustine Kandathil in the foreword dated 13 May 1946; catalogue’s 1945 date is not followed.
stages.scope: Editorial arrangement and specified additions verified in original preliminary leaves.
stages.summary: Regroups and brackets transferred material, supplies proper and server texts, and preserves a Nineveh appendix with Marian Huthama.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Chaldaicus rituum et lectionum, reditus a P. Matthaeo Vadakel, Mar Thoma Sleeha, Alwaye, 1946

evidence.claim: Identifies the Latin consultative text and its component page ranges.

stages.label: Latin study text for restoration
stages.limitations: Book not acquired. Publication in 1955 is distinct from approval on 26 June 1957 and reception in 1962.
stages.reception: Roman commission study text; not asserted to have been used as a Latin-language altar missal.
stages.scope: Consultative formulation of the original reform, not a lay translation lineage.
stages.summary: Contains the common order, three anaphoras and forms of celebration for episcopal consultation.
stages.witness_label: Liturgia Siro-Malabaresi: Revisione e Ristampa del Messale Siro-Malabarese, Rome 1955, Prot. 947/48

evidence.claim: Distinguishes the approved three-anaphora programme, companion books, and narrower 12 May 1960 Syriac printing.
Lists the three books as publications of the restoration.
The Syriac Taksa d-Quddasha printed at Alwaye in 1960, with Archbishop Joseph Parecattil's imprimatur of 12 May 1960, is present as a separately titled 62-page part of the 1962 book.

evidence.claim: The Latin proper volume, Prot. N. 947/48, Rome 1960, imprimatur 5 January 1960, has an index of Hudra items beginning on pp. 3-163 and Gazza items beginning on pp. 169-257 (start pages of entries, not part extents).
evidence.locus: PDF 1 title; PDF 2 imprimatur 5 January 1960; PDF 5 index

evidence.claim: The 20 January 1962 instruction names the three books issued after the papal approval of 26 June 1957: the Syriac Taksa d-Quddasha with the ordinary and the anaphora of Addai and Mari, the Latin Ordo celebrationis Quddasa regulating three forms of celebration, and the Latin Supplementum Mysteriorum.
evidence.locus: Document 30, printed 207; Latin Appendix I, printed 387

stages.label: Restoration issued in complementary books
stages.limitations: The 1960 Syriac Taksa is now seen through its title, imprimatur and 62 pages as bound in the 1962 book, and the Supplementum through its title, imprimatur, preface and index; the Latin 1959 Ordo celebrationis is still unseen, and no body text is collated. The CMS file labelled 1959 is a 1998 translation. Companion volumes must not become sequential whole-missal revisions.
stages.reception: Programme approved by Pius XII in 1957; its complete contents were not all introduced in worship in 1962.
stages.scope: Rubrics/calendar, propers and a restricted Syriac ordinary issued separately.
stages.summary: The three books supply different components; the Syriac ordinary includes only Addai and Mari in the simple form.
stages.witness_label: Ordo celebrationis Quddasa (Rome 1959); Supplementum Mysteriorum (Rome 1960); Taksa d’Quddasa (Alwaye 1960)

evidence.claim: Separates 20 January promulgation from 3 July introduction and identifies omitted components.
Identifies bilingual publication and continuing Syriac passages.

stages.label: Partial restoration introduced in worship
stages.limitations: A reception stage, not a new original-language revision inferred from translation. The 1962 instruction is read in a documentary edition's Latin text, not in the archival original; the bilingual book's Malayalam body is not collated.
stages.reception: Syro-Malabar episcopal introduction; not proof of uniform practice in every parish.
stages.scope: Community reception of the restricted restored order in the approved 1962 Syriac–Malayalam Qurbana book; its operative Malayalam text is received service-book language, while this stage remains limited to the partial restoration introduced in worship.
stages.summary: The bishops introduced the bilingual order on 3 July; several approved restored components remained unimplemented.

evidence.claim: Confirms year, typical-edition designation and native Syriac content.
evidence.locus: Physical PDF 3–5, English/Syriac title leaves and first rubric leaf

evidence.claim: A second copy reproduces the same Syriac title leaf and the Syriac order of Qurbana from printed 12 to its close at about printed 57, including a separately headed Order of the Fraction and Consignation at printed 42.
evidence.locus: PDF 1 Syriac title leaf; PDF 2 = printed 12; PDF 36 = printed 42; PDF 57 (number cut off; follows printed 56)

stages.label: 2003 Syriac typical-edition witness
stages.limitations: Provisional because no approval decree, preface or changed-text statement has been found in either the CMS excerpt or the Internet Archive copy, and the body has not been collated against the 1960 Syriac Taksa (now held through the 1962 book) or the 1985/1989 orders. Do not count as an established substantive new stage from the title and body alone.
stages.reception: Title says use of the Church of the East Syrians of Malabar; Catholic bibliographic context corroborated by commission-hosted source list.
stages.scope: Identified 2003 Syriac typical-edition printing whose order of Qurbana body (printed 12 to about 57) is now held; approval act, front matter and predecessor comparison unresolved.
stages.summary: Title identifies the Malabar use and Addai–Mari anaphora; native Syriac leaves are visible.
stages.witness_label: Order of the Mysteries with the First Hallowing of Mar Addai and Mar Mari, Editio Typica, Rome 2003

evidence.claim: Reassembles gatherings of O across the three shelfmarks; the print also uses other material.

The Vatican part of the reconstructed manuscript shows encircled invocation passages and a Latin marginal note on the epiclesis on the folio Jabbour cites (f. 45r); the marked Syriac was not transcribed, so its correspondence to Jabbour's correction layers is not checked here.

stages.label: Manuscript O before Roman editing
stages.limitations: Reconstruction attributed to Jabbour; surviving manuscripts and colophon not inspected. It is not a complete uncontested single-parent genealogy. 2026-10-21: one Vatican opening (f. 45) was inspected; the Florence parts and the colophon remain uninspected.
stages.reception: Maronite manuscript provenance; date of its dispatch to Rome is disputed. The later printed uniform formula must not be projected back over all manuscript layers.
stages.scope: Source manuscript identified by Jabbour, including the pre-editing institution and epiclesis layers; not all precursors of the print.
stages.summary: A divided 1566 missal used in preparing the first print; supplements also contributed.
stages.witness_label: Mikhail al-Rizzi’s manuscript O: Florence BNCF Cl.III.79 and Cl.III.74, with Vatican Vat.sir.431; colophon BNCF Cl.III.74 f 154r–v.

evidence.claim: Latin 1594 and Syriac 1592 dates coexist in this physical witness; 1594 dedication and examiner colophon are visible.
Describes fourteen anaphoras and alteration of institution and epiclesis.
Identifies Sixtus first and the inclusion of Sharar.

stages.label: First print with revised institution and epicleses
stages.limitations: Liturgical body not transcribed or collated. Dual title dates do not establish two successive textual states.
stages.reception: Dib reports introduction at the 1596 synod with Dandini. Beggiani records initial prohibition and later permission while manuscript formulas continued locally; neither account proves universal immediate replacement.
stages.scope: Roman first printing, bounded by checked paratext and source-described liturgical revision.
stages.summary: Fourteen anaphoras; Sixtus first and Sharar included. Institution wording standardized; epiclesis petitions altered.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum iuxta ritum Ecclesiae nationis Maronitarum, Romae in Typographia Medicea; IA bub_gb_5Eqy8WGF9aQC.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes alpha copies marking names from beta copies substituting them.
Confirms a 1608 reimpression with textual changes and new Du Perron preface.

stages.label: Reprint variant replacing commemorated names
stages.limitations: No 1608 copy independently collated. Jabbour warns that editions may be impressions; alpha/beta is his analytical grouping, not a new universal liturgical edition.
stages.reception: Presence in surviving copies establishes a printed variant; no community-wide reception date established.
stages.scope: Specific diptych/commemoration revision in Jabbour’s beta group; not every 1608 copy.
stages.summary: One 1608 group substitutes Maron, Antony, Jacob and Ephrem for earlier commemorated names.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum 1608 reimpressions, beta group in Jabbour’s comparison; BnF RES M-B-3 is a separately identified 1608 reissue, not assigned here to beta.

evidence.claim: Reports altered roster, fourteen total, Roman Church and Sharar-derived Good Friday order.
Explains adaptation of Roman Canon material to the structure of Twelve Apostles.

Quotes the 1716 preface on compiling a Roman Church anaphora, placing John Maron's anaphora last and the Sharar-derived signing of the chalice after the anaphoras; gives the contents as the Mass with thirteen anaphoras then the signing-of-the-chalice anaphora, Gospel selections (103) and weekday Epistles; tabulates the first-edition roster of fourteen against the second edition's retentions and replacements; reports printing in Rome 1715 with a closing note dating completion to 1716.

Official retrospective: the second printing of 1716 also had fourteen, dropping three of the first printing and adding John Maron, Roman Church and a different Chrysostom text, and turned Sharar into the Mass of the signing of the chalice.

stages.label: Roman-derived anaphora and Good Friday adaptation
stages.limitations: No 1716 page images inspected; the roster is from scholarship (Gemayel's full table, Kaufhold's partial copy description, Feulner) and two official retrospectives. Thirteen versus fourteen corresponds in Gemayel's description to whether the signing-of-the-chalice order is counted, but Dib and Feulner do not state their basis. Gemayel quotes the preface as placing the Roman Church anaphora after Xystus; the full printed order is not settled here. The Roman Church anaphora should not be described merely as an unchanged translation of the Roman Canon.
stages.reception: Publication and later reception are distinct. Synodal debates about institution wording do not independently identify a new missal state.
stages.scope: Second Roman missal revision described in multiple histories.
stages.summary: Fourteen items in the roster according to Dib, the 2005 presentation and Gemayel's table, counted as thirteen anaphoras followed by the signing-of-the-chalice order by Gemayel; Feulner counts thirteen. The roster changes: Roman Church added (in place of Marutha), John Maron added (in place of John bar Shushan), a second, different Chrysostom text replaces the first; Sharar removed as an anaphora and adapted as the Good Friday signing of the chalice.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syriacum iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Antiochenae nationis Maronitarum, Rome, Propaganda Fide 1716.

stages.date_label: 1762 title imprint; approbation 10 April 1763 (same copy); 1763 in the official introduction

evidence.claim: Title 1762 and approbation 1763 stand on one copy; the book has eight anaphoras with institution narratives and a separately headed Good Friday chalice-signing order.
evidence.locus: Canvas 430 title; canvas 3 approbation; anaphora headings canvases 226, 196, 183, 156, 137, 116, 103, 094; Good Friday heading canvas 072 with running heads 040-071

evidence.claim: Dates third edition 1762–63 and counts nine.
Counts nine and identifies first anaphora as Second Peter.
Reports eight for 1763.
The printer's note dates completion of printing in Rome to 2 Nisan (April) under Clement XIII, year read tentatively as 1763; canvas 116 heads the anaphora of Eustathius.

Third edition 1763 (a copy in the Oriental Library, Beirut): preface says the 1716 book was exhausted and the Antonine procurator Fr Thomas reprinted it at the order's expense; five anaphoras omitted (Matthew the Shepherd, Dionysius, Eustathius, John Chrysostom, Cyril); closing note dates completion to 2 April 1763; Assemani's approbation of 10 April 1763; not sealed by the patriarch; Gospels placed in the Mass and year beginning with Consecration Sunday.

stages.label: Reduced anaphora repertoire
stages.limitations: Eight anaphoras plus the Good Friday item are what the inspected copy contains. Gemayel's count of five omissions leaves the same total, but he names Eustathius among the omitted, while the ONB copy has an Eustathius heading (canvas 116, re-viewed) and no heading for James; this is either an error in one account or a variant issue, and is not resolved. That a count of nine includes the Good Friday item is compatible but not stated by Dib or Beggiani. The approbation's statement of agreement with 1716 is a doctrinal approval formula, not evidence of an unchanged repertoire. The lectionary and calendar arrangement rests on Gemayel and was not checked on the ONB images. Body text not transcribed; one copy, variant issues unchecked.
stages.reception: Subsequent Lebanese printings are reported; continuity of every wording or rubric has not been collated.
stages.scope: Third Roman edition with smaller repertoire; disputed exact count retained.
stages.summary: Repertoire reduced from the 1716 book. The inspected copy carries eight anaphora headings, each with its own institution narrative: Peter head of the Apostles, Twelve Apostles, Xystus, John, Mark, Eustathius, the holy Roman Church and John Maron. A separate Good Friday order headed as the anaphora of the signing of the holy chalice follows them. Gemayel describes the edition as a reprint of 1716 at the Antonine order's expense omitting five anaphoras, with Gospel texts at their place in the Mass and a liturgical year beginning with the Sunday of the Consecration of the Church. Dib and Beggiani count nine; the 1992 introduction counts eight.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syriacum juxta ritum Ecclesiae Antiochenae nationis Syrorum Maronitarum, Rome, Komarek 1762 (approbation 10 April 1763); ONB 22.D.32 ALT PRUNK.

evidence.claim: Fourth to seventh editions (1816, 1838, 1855, 1872) from the Qozhaya press copy the third edition's texts with simple linguistic corrections and a changed movable-feast table, append daily Gospel selections after Farhat, change the start of the year, keep the older front calendar alongside Farhat's saints, and name the patriarch (1838 colophon quoted).

stages.label: Qozhaya printing with appended daily Gospel selections
stages.limitations: No Qozhaya copy inspected; the change is source-described by Gemayel, who does not say in which of the four printings the Gospel appendix first appears beyond grouping them as the fourth edition onwards. The 1838, 1855 and 1872 printings are not counted as further states. Cold review 2026-10-22: Gemayel ties the January year start explicitly to the fourth edition onward, but the Gospel appendix and the replacement of the Roman approvals are features of the Qozhaya group, the latter shown only from 1838.
stages.reception: Printed by the Lebanese monks with the patriarch's permission according to the quoted 1838 colophon; not sealed by the patriarch (Gemayel p. 65). Local use is not established.
stages.scope: Lebanese reprint line of the 1763 text at the press of St Anthony, Qozhaya, as described by Gemayel; lectionary and calendar arrangement only.
stages.summary: Reprints the 1763 liturgical texts with small linguistic corrections, appends Gospel selections for every day of the year after Germanos Farhat, and begins the year with January and the first Sunday after Epiphany instead of the Sunday of the Consecration of the Church; among other small changes of the Qozhaya printings, the patriarch's name takes the place of the Roman approvals, illustrated by Gemayel only from the 1838 colophon.
stages.witness_label: Qurbono (Liber oblationis), press of the monastery of St Anthony Qozhaya, Lebanese monks, 1816; the 1838, 1855 and 1872 Qozhaya printings are reported as reprints of the same line.

evidence.claim: Second Peter leads the preceding edition; Debs 1888 places Roman Church first.
Identifies the 1908 second printing and its retained title page.
Order in the 1908 printing: Roman Church, Peter, Twelve Apostles, Mark, John, Xystus, Eustathius, John Maron.

Eighth edition, Maronite Press Beirut 1888, by Archbishop Joseph Dibs after consulting Patriarch Paul Mas'ad; quotes the preface: Roman anaphora placed first with the common prayers, rubrics translated from Syriac into Arabic, directions from Latin books added, Gospel/Epistle translations revised, Augustinian preparation and thanksgiving prayers, calendar 1889-2000; ninth edition 1908 identical except for added celebration directions (Manara).

stages.label: Dibs order with Roman Church first
stages.limitations: 1888 itself not seen; its contents come from Dibs's preface as quoted by Gemayel and from Beggiani. Gemayel states that the 1908 printing matches 1888 in everything except the added directions, which is consistent with the 1908 anaphora order being that of 1888, but he lists no anaphora orders; the moves of Xystus, Mark and John are observed only between the 1762 and 1908 witnesses. The 1888 date is publication, not the duration of use. Cold review 2026-10-22: Gemayel (p. 61) judges that this edition changed nothing of substance beyond correcting wording, putting the Roman anaphora first and multiplying Latin-style directions; Dibs's preface says he neglected some prayers and blessings and abbreviated others, and the monthly calendar was only translated into Arabic with its feasts unchanged. The added components record these preface-described features, not a reform.
stages.reception: Dibs reports consulting the patriarch; Gemayel notes that no edition bears the patriarch's seal. The 1908 printing is a witness to the Dibs line, not a separately proved reform.
stages.scope: Dibs’s reorder, witnessed bibliographically by 1888 and 1908; no separate 1908 revision established.
stages.summary: Roman Church replaces Peter at the head of the anaphora sequence; the 1908 printing has the same eight anaphoras as 1762 in a new order. Dibs's preface, as quoted by Gemayel, also reports Arabic translation of the rubrics and added directions taken from Latin books, a revised Arabic rendering of the audible prayers and readings, preparation and thanksgiving prayers, and an annual calendar for 1889-2000.
stages.witness_label: Yusuf al-Dibs, Beirut missal 1888; Ketābā de-qurbānā, al-Maṭbaʿa al-Mārūnīya 1908, second printing.

evidence.claim: Lists the differences of the 1959 tenth edition from the previous edition and describes its uncertain authority.
Printed by the Lebanese Missionary Fathers of Jounieh in 1959; replaced Garshuni with Arabic; never received official approval.

stages.label: Unofficial practical edition in Arabic script
stages.limitations: The 1959 book was not seen; the changes are Gemayel's description. Not a new recension of the anaphoras; whether any material was newly composed in Arabic is not established. Cold review 2026-10-22: kept as a documented state because the book-state layer admits an identifiable edition without an approval act and Gemayel's paged description shows changes to rubrics, prayers and end matter beyond the script change; it is not an approved book, unlike the bkerke2005 stage on another deferred candidate, and must not be read as an authorized Maronite missal.
stages.reception: Gemayel reports that copies carry different or no authorizations, that some bishops forbade its use, and that it nevertheless spread to almost all churches; Beggiani says it never received official approval. No approval act is claimed.
stages.scope: Unofficial practical edition described by Gemayel; changes to rubrics, ordinary prayers and end matter, not a new anaphora repertoire.
stages.summary: Drops the prefaces, prints all Garshuni in Arabic script, shortens or removes rubrical directions, puts some hymns and prayers in Arabic, deletes some prayers (the Proemion and first Sedro of the first office, the incense prayer for the dead at the end of Mass, some closing prayers), adds feast psalms before the Epistle, and drops the end matter (preparation and thanksgiving prayers, blessings and the annual calendar). Gemayel calls it a hasty commercial practical printing that spread to almost all churches without official permission.
stages.witness_label: Tenth edition of the Maronite Mass book, Al-Karim press of the Lebanese Missionaries (Jounieh), 1959, as described by Gemayel; title page not seen.

evidence.claim: Separates 1972 Roman proposal from the 1973 patriarchal experiment.
The patriarch's account of the post-conciliar revision names only the abbreviated rite approved by Patriarch Meouchi and put in force by decree 43/1973; it mentions no 1972 Roman text.

stages.label: Roman experimental proposal
stages.limitations: Deliberately provisional. Only Beggiani (p. 20, re-viewed 2026-10-22) reports the 1972 proposal of the Congregation for the Eastern Churches, a one-year experimental text with the Twelve Apostles as its only anaphora; no text, decree, letter or copy has been located, and the original Arabic 2005 introduction does not mention it. Gemayel's 1970 study predates it. It cannot be merged with 1973 or used to identify the 1973 anaphora.
stages.reception: Proposal and authorized local adoption require separate evidence.
stages.scope: A proposal described by Beggiani, requiring identification of its exact text and enactment.
stages.summary: One-year experiment containing Twelve Apostles alone.
stages.witness_label: Experimental text proposed by the Congregation for the Eastern Churches; exact 1972 book identity not inspected.

evidence.claim: Identifies 1973 Simple Rite as a one-anaphora experiment.
Identifies a distinct 1973 patriarchal text retaining Roman institution wording.

evidence.locus: PDF 6 (2005 patriarchal introduction, English; the Arabic counterpart follows)

evidence.claim: Original Arabic: the commission revised the Maronite Mass rite approved by Patriarch Paul Peter Meouchi with the consent of the patriarchal synod, an abbreviated rite put into effect by decree no. 43/1973 issued 13 April 1973 for one year as an experiment; from 1975 the wars interrupted the commission's work and unapproved variant rites appeared.

stages.label: Patriarchal experimental simple rite
stages.limitations: No original 1973 booklet or decree inspected; decree number and date are now read in the original Arabic 2005 introduction as well as its 2012 reproduction, both later patriarchal sources. Exact identity of the single anaphora is not safely supplied from Beggiani's description of 1972.
stages.reception: Experimental permission is not perpetual universal promulgation. Neither source establishes identical local reception everywhere.
stages.scope: Experimental simple rite; full institution text and relation to 1972 remain unchecked.
stages.summary: A restricted experimental book; the official introduction reports one anaphora.
stages.witness_label: Simple Rite issued by the Maronite Patriarchate in 1973, described by the 1992 introduction.

stages.label: Reformed six-anaphora Qurbono
stages.limitations: Primary reform explanation, not a full transcription. Comprehensive Old/New Testament lectionary was still being prepared; later complementary Gospel/Epistle books are not successive missal versions.

The 2005 book (printed p. 20) calls the 1992 book the first printing, which was under trial, and its own rite the fixed rite until further notice.
stages.scope: Syriac/Arabic reform represented by the contemporary commission introduction and later commentary.
stages.summary: Six anaphoras: Twelve Apostles, Peter, James, John, Mark, Sixtus; expanded annual services.
stages.witness_label: Book of Offering according to the Tradition of the Antiochene Syriac Maronite Church, Bkerke 1992.

stages.date_label: 2005; patriarchal decree 29 June 2005, in use from the first Sunday of November 2005

evidence.claim: Approval chain, effective and exclusive-use dates, and the description of the book as the second edition of the revised ritual.
The edition translated from Bkerke 2005 has eight anaphoras with the names listed.

Body not transcribed. Anaphora names do not show whether texts of the same name match earlier printings.
stages.reception: The decree prescribes use throughout the patriarchal territory and the diaspora from November 2005 and exclusive use from 25 December 2005; actual uniform use is not established. The 2003-2006 synod separately requires the approved Mass order.
stages.scope: Patriarchal approval of the revised Mass book called its second printing; decree, introductions, structure and anaphora headings read in the original Arabic people's volume of 2005, the celebrant's bilingual volumes not seen.
stages.summary: Decree 1512/2005 approves the new printing after the Congregation for the Eastern Churches' letter 381/2003 of 17 April 2005 and synodal consent, orders its use from the first Sunday of November 2005 and forbids any other Mass book from 25 December 2005. Eight anaphoras: Twelve Apostles, Peter, James, John, Mark, Xystus, John Chrysostom and John Maron; obligatory Syriac texts, including the institution prayer, in an appendix of the people's volume.
stages.witness_label: Kitab al-Quddas according to the rite of the Antiochene Syriac Maronite Church, Kitab al-Mu'minin, Bkerke 2005 (1117 printed pages; Internet Archive Maronite_Missal; seminary library Tl 188 Ar has the same page count), with the 2012 approved English edition.

evidence.claim: Explicitly distinguishes the approved Mass order from complementary reading, chant and directions books; sets celebration and Holy Week prescriptions.

stages.limitations: No new complete missal recension is inferred from the synodal date. The before-state and first introduction of these rubrics are not established here; no revision edge is drawn.
stages.reception: The synodal directions encompass the patriarchal territory and diaspora in the document’s account of the liturgical commission. Prescribed unity does not establish uniform empirical use.
stages.scope: Eucharistic legislation governing approved books and celebration; a reception witness alongside printed missals.
stages.summary: The synod directs exclusive use of the Mass order approved by the synod and patriarchal decree, alongside separately issued Epistle and Gospel books, chant book and ritual directions. It prefers concelebration at the principal altar, prescribes the Presanctified on Good Friday and no Mass on Holy Saturday.
stages.witness_label: Maronite Patriarchal Synod, Text 12: Liturgy, official Arabic text on Bkerki.org

stages.label: Monza H14 local Roman ceremonial order
stages.limitations: No complete H14 text, original manuscript collation, exact copying year, promulgation act or revision is established. Liber ordinarius is an order book; its title does not identify a Mass Ordinary. Frisi associated copying with a 1256 bequest; that older report is not used to narrow the modern broad century range.
stages.reception: The local order prescribes ceremonial practice for Monza. Frisi's local title attribution rests on still-legible erased wording; the census and edition review separately support H14 identity and classification. No first celebration, uniform observance or continuity through 1578 is established.

stages.limitations: No direct 35.3 images acquired. Exact contributions to 1991/1994 remain uncollated.
stages.reception: Evidence of a medieval Hispanic source tradition, later used in critical reconstruction; no continuous or exclusive modern reception inferred.
stages.scope: Individually identified priestly euchology witness, mediated by a critical edition and later scholarship; exact manuscript date remains unresolved.
stages.summary: Tradition A is now represented by an identified manuscript witness, without a false A→B succession.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes A/B; attributes printed books to B; names the 1500 missal and its retained Creed/fraction sequence.
Reprints the completion date 9 January 1500, Toledo printer and Ortiz’s role.

evidence.claim: Describes the 1500 Ordo as Hispanic formulas adapted to a Roman Toledan order with priestly apologies.

Complete source-defined Benedictio panis independently image-collated and bound as nine native text units, with declared reading normalization; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.

evidence.claim: Ordo core from the rubric before Adesto through the Liberati embolism, including the two variable Advent I prayers printed inside it (post pridie; ad orationem dominicam), independently image-collated and bound as twenty native text units with declared reading normalization; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.

stages.label: Cisneros’s printed Toledan missal
stages.limitations: Exact 9 January 1500 publication date is directly inspected in the original colophon, in addition to its 1755 reprint. All 973 offered image positions are retained, but the full book has not been transcribed or collated and physical completeness is not independently established. Native text bindings cover only the complete bread blessing and the Ordo core printed in Dominica prima de adventu (positions 31-34), including its two variable Advent I prayers. The Roman-source dating differs in emphasis between 1988 (thirteenth-century copies) and 2014 (fifteenth-century usage); no false reconciliation.
stages.reception: Cisneros established the Corpus Christi chapel for daily Mass and Office; the 1988 account also notes earlier parish use. No claim that every manuscript or parish followed this printed recension.
stages.scope: Latin printed Mass book compiling the Toledan B tradition under Alfonso Ortiz; whole-book identity, with order evidence supplied by official retrospectives.
stages.summary: The print consolidates B-based materials used by the Saints Justa and Rufina community. Its Order retains Creed before fraction and Lord’s Prayer, while adding Roman devotional material to Hispanic formulas. The printed compilation is an editorial state with partly lost manuscript exemplars.

text_projections.title: Mozarabic Ordo missae core, 1500 (Dominica prima de adventu): complete constituent

stages.witness_label: Missale mixtum secundum regulam beati Isidori dictum Mozarabes; Toledo 1500

evidence.claim: Identifies edition, sampled Mass body, terminal bread blessing and scholarly appendix.
Calls 1755 a re-edition with Lesley’s presentation and explanatory notes; identifies PL 85 as a reproduction of it.
Complete source-defined Benedictio panis independently image-collated and bound as nine native text units, with declared reading normalization; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.
evidence.locus: Printed p. 471, original source image 590 / PDF page 591

evidence.claim: Ordo core from the rubric before Adesto through the Liberati embolism, including the two variable Advent I prayers printed inside it (post pridie; ad orationem dominicam), independently image-collated and bound as twenty native text units with declared reading normalization; Lesley's line numbers excluded; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.
evidence.locus: Printed pp. 5-6 (NYPL/Google copy images 0127-0128; Florence image 0123 for the marginal note)

stages.label: Lesley’s annotated republication
stages.limitations: No whole-body 1500/1755 collation or substantive ritual revision is claimed. The entire offered Florence PDF is retained; only the complete nine-unit Benedictio panis, using the sharper original JPEG2000 page, and the Ordo core printed in Dominica prima de adventu (pp. 5-6) are bound as native text. The Ordo core is read from the NYPL digitization of the same edition, whose full-resolution pages are legible where the Florence images are 685 pixels wide; only its gutter-cropped marginal note is read on the Florence page. Comparison preserves the presbiter/presbyter orthographic difference without treating it as a new prayer version.
stages.reception: A scholarly republication of the Toledan printed tradition. Its publication alone does not demonstrate substitution in every celebrating community.
stages.scope: Republication with extensive historical preface, explanatory notes and appendices; representative liturgical pages and terminal blessing checked.
stages.summary: Lesley gives the inherited printed missal a scholarly apparatus. The inspected body includes Advent IV’s variable euchology and blessing; Benedictio panis stands at p 471 before the original colophon and later notes. Appendix prima prints a Mass attributed to St Pelagius from Sandoval; an appendix is not automatically part of the prescribed liturgical body.

text_projections.title: Mozarabic Ordo missae core, 1755 (Dominica prima de adventu): complete constituent

stages.witness_label: Missale mixtum, Alexander Lesley; Rome, Monaldini / typis Joannis Generosi Salomoni, 1755

evidence.locus: Printed cols. 12-17, BSB canvases 28-31 (Dominica prima de adventu)

stages.label: Lorenzana–Arévalo corrected missal
stages.limitations: Exact selected pages, the complete nine-unit bread blessing and the Ordo core printed in Dominica prima de adventu (cols. 12-17) are checked; the acquired and hashed 744082515-byte complete PDF remains remote for its measured size. No full-lineage or exhaustive text-change count is claimed. Do not confuse this edition with PL 85’s 1862 reprint of 1755. Edition dependence and changed blessing placement do not by themselves identify the immediate textual parent of this constituent.
stages.reception: Contemporary 1988 reform introduction reports daily use of the 1804 book in Toledo’s Mozarabic chapel. This attests use in 1988; it does not establish a universal 1804 effective date or uninterrupted use everywhere.
stages.scope: Corrected edition of the inherited printed missal, with relocated blessing and reused/augmented scholarly apparatus.
stages.summary: Arévalo completed Lorenzana’s posthumous edition. The title calls it recognized and reprinted; Arévalo explains his reuse of Lesley’s dissertation and notes, addition of his own notes and attempted correction of faulty or obscure readings, with further manuscript collation left to readers who had access. Benedictio panis now precedes the Temporal at p XVI.

evidence.claim: Defines the corpus and concrete reform operations.

evidence.claim: Describes commission changes and final confirmation.
Official decree summary: Latin text of the Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum approved for Spain, 23 January 1994, Prot. CD 763/92.
Three personal faculties of 5 October 1994 (Prot. 857/94/L, 861/94/L, 862/94/L) for named priests to celebrate Mass in the Hispano-Mozarabic rite; grants, not attested celebrations.

stages.label: Critical missal incorporating both traditions
stages.limitations: No protected modern full book was acquired or transcribed. Change evidence is primary-description, not line-by-line collation. The 1988 design envisaged a separate Order volume; exact final binding and every volume table of contents remain uninspected. The two publication years are not two replacement editions. Notitiae 29 (1993) p. 726 lists Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum and Liber Commicus (Conferencia Episcopal Española, Arzobispado de Toledo, Coeditores Litúrgicos, Barcelona 1991) under the 17 July 1988 confirmation with the language field 'hispanica'; whether that field denotes Spanish-language volumes or misdescribes the Latin books is not established, and the notice supplies no title-leaf data.
stages.reception: Prepared for living Catholic Hispano-Mozarabic communities. The 1988 introduction names Toledo chapel/parish context; no present-day universal permission or precise effective date is inferred from bibliographical notices. Notitiae 30 (1994) p. 544 records three personal faculties of 5 October 1994 to celebrate Mass in the Hispano-Mozarabic rite, granted to a diocesan priest of Mallorca, a Claretian and a Piarist (Prot. 857/94/L, 861/94/L and 862/94/L); the grants name no place of celebration and are not attested celebrations. On 28 May 1992 John Paul II celebrated Mass in this rite in the Vatican Basilica (Notitiae 28 (1992) p. 404), and on 28 December 1993 a further personal faculty was granted to Pere Farnés Scherer of Barcelona (Prot. 2441/93/L, Notitiae 29 (1993) p. 688). These are single celebrations or grants, not evidence of general use.
stages.scope: Completed complementary Latin missal corpus, positioned at the second tome’s 1994 publication; first tome published in 1991. Calendar, revised Order, Temporal, saints’ Proper/Common, deceased and votive Masses; readings and chants drawn from both traditions.
stages.summary: The reform retains B’s Creed–fraction–Lord’s Prayer order but reconstructs the Order with A evidence, removes inherited Roman devotional additions and supplies optional quiet prayers from the Hispanic Liber ordinum. Both traditions expand the readings, chant texts and euchology; selected celebrations have Year I/II variants, sometimes including Triduum structure. Latin readings use the Neovulgate.
stages.witness_label: Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum, CEE / Archdiocese of Toledo, 1991 and 1994

evidence.claim: Names the 1995 Proprium de Sanctis companion and confirmation date.
Identifies Missale and Liber Commicus as paired products of the commission, each in two volumes.

stages.reception: Companion book of the Catholic Hispano-Mozarabic reform. Separate publication and shared confirmation do not establish a new whole-missal revision or autonomous rite.
stages.scope: The saints-volume witness of the Liber Commicus companion to the reformed missal; part of a two-volume reading corpus, not a successor missal.
stages.summary: The separately published lectionary supplies the reading component of the same reform. This stage dates the directly verified 1995 Latin saints-volume witness; the official 1996 notice reports 23 January 1994 confirmation.

The two named blessings are added 'prout in usu' (as customary), so they do not evidence a change from earlier Lyon practice or from the 1866 book; the decree establishes an approved edition, not a textual state shown to differ from 1866. stages.label: Roman Missal revised under Pius V
stages.limitations: The title and colophon identify the original Rome 1570 printing; 14 July Quo primum remains an act date, not its exact printing day. No full textual delta from 1474 is proven. The Ritus final-blessing directions differ from the separate Venice 1570 witness, so that witness cannot silently supply the Roman baseline. Exempt older uses are not incorporated. The native text binding completes only the strict Canon on printed pp. 281–286 under its declared reading normalization; the remainder of the wider running-head section and whole Missal remain untranscribed. An independent re-reading of the Rome 1570 Canon images on 2026-10-22 (batch-5 text-roman cold review) found that the bound reading departs from the print at several loci: it reads Et quotquot where the print has Ut quotquot (p. 285); in the doxology it omits et before in ipso, places in ipso after the rubric and reads inter seipsum, where the print has et in ipso before the rubric bis signat inter pectus et calicem (p. 286); it reads operit for co-operit (p. 286); it omits the printed Amen after the Memento of the dead (p. 285), et between surgit and ostendit (p. 284) and the red Iungit manus beside the closing staff (p. 286); and its capitals do not consistently follow the print. The binding needs re-collation before text differences from it are used.

stages.label: Urbanian corrected missal

Preliminaries, terminal leaves and the Canon (printed pp. 245-249) were viewed; the Canon is word-compared with the Rome 1604 Canon, but no reading-level or rubric-by-rubric collation of the rest of the book with 1604 is claimed. A bounded 2026-10-22 search (Internet Archive, Google Books catalogue feed, HathiTrust and Gallica refused, SBN OPAC not machine-readable) found no 1634-dated Rome issue. The native text binding completes only the strict Canon on printed pp. 245-249 of the 1635 witness under its declared reading normalization; the remainder of the Missal remains untranscribed.
