stages.limitations: A complete public NSK image copy of the 1631 book is now located and its title inspected, but its body has not been read; no actual-use abolition or exact prayer/rubric delta claimed. Need precise target source/prayer collation; no immediate 1483 parent.
stages.reception: Prescription, printing and regional reception are separate. No universal implementation date asserted.
stages.scope: Missal-level normative revision and replacement prescription, not enumerated prayer changes.
stages.summary: Ecclesia catholica mandates a missal corrected against the Pius V and Clement VIII Roman emendations, from multiple Dalmatian Slavonic missals. It prohibits use of older printed/manuscript Slavonic books and prescribes new book or Latin after eight months from Roman publication.
stages.witness_label: Urban VIII revision mandate for Slavonic Roman missal

evidence.claim: Original title and calendar rows read for occupancy, dates and red/black entries.

stages.label: Calendar of the 1631 Levaković Slavonic Roman missal
stages.limitations: Row occupancy and dates were read directly; the Glagolitic saint names were not transliterated. Other months and the proper of saints were not compared. Same printed book as slavonic-roman:1631, whose row is dated by the Urban VIII mandate; this row records the printed calendar for the 1631→1741 comparison and is not a second 1631 version.
stages.reception: Printed book state; regional adoption is a separate question.
stages.scope: Printed calendar at the inspected months (October and November), with the title leaf; not the whole book.
stages.summary: The printed 1631 calendar leaves 2 October and 13, 14, 15, 16 and 20 November without entries, and gives single entries on 10, 19 and 24 November.
stages.witness_label: NSK RIIA-4-2a, Missal rimskij va ezik slovenskij, Rome 1631

evidence.claim: Redaction description and original title photo checked.

Original 1741 Latin title and imprint directly inspected; the holding library transcribes the Glagolitic title as slavenskim êzykom, against va ezik slovenskij for 1631 (catalogue transcriptions, Glagolitic not read here).
Calendar rows with Mass page references read directly and compared with 1631.
evidence.locus: Canvas 38 (printed p. 34, October); canvas 39 (printed p. 35, November)

stages.label: Karaman/Sović 1741 Slavonic Roman missal with an expanded calendar
stages.limitations: Documented as a calendar state from inspected primary pages; the East Slavonic redaction and the appendix remain Lokmer's description. Saint names in the added rows were not transliterated, so identifications are by date only. The pro aliquibus locis appendix was not identified in the composite NSK copy, and ordinary and rubric changes are uncollated.
stages.reception: Prescription, printing and regional reception are separate. No universal implementation date asserted.
stages.scope: Printed 1741 edition: inspected title and calendar months; linguistic redaction attributed to scholarship.
stages.summary: The 1741 Rome edition adds calendar entries absent from the 1631 printing (2 October; 13, 15 and 20 November) and gives new first-named feasts on 10, 19 and 24 November. Copy-based scholarship reports a complete East Slavonic linguistic recension and an initial pro aliquibus locis appendix; a later 1789 supplement is separately bound.
stages.witness_label: Karaman/Sović East Slavonic redaction candidate

evidence.claim: Original title 1893 and printing permission 25 January 1893 directly visible.

Title states recognition under Leo XIII's authority; the front matter reprints the Pius V, Clement VIII and Urban VIII acts and later Congregation decrees signed by Cardinal Patrizi (citing Pius VII and Pius IX); no separate Leo XIII act was seen.
October and November calendar rows read directly; 20 October, 14 November and 26 November compared with 1741.
evidence.locus: PDF 29 (printed p. XXI) and PDF 30 (printed p. XXII)

evidence.claim: Attributed linguistic restoration characterization.

The 1896 issue reprints the January 1893 permission with no new approval at the inspected front leaves, and its October–November calendar agrees with 1893 at the compared rows; whether its text differs elsewhere (Lokmer reports a longer sanctoral) is unverified.

stages.label: Parčić 1893 Glagolitic Roman missal recognized under Leo XIII
stages.limitations: Documented as an inspected title, permission and calendar state. No exact body wording has been collated against 1741 or the Latin typical edition of 1884; the permission is not evidence of an independent Latin recension, and the linguistic restoration remains the institute's description. The book prints no statement of what was changed beyond the title and calendar. 1896/1905 are not automatically distinct.
stages.reception: Prescription, printing and regional reception are separate. No universal implementation date asserted.
stages.scope: Printed 1893 edition: inspected title, Propaganda printing permission, Glagolitic papal front matter and October–November calendar; linguistic restoration attributed to scholarship; Latin source-recension identity unresolved.
stages.summary: The title presents the missal as edited by order of Pius V and recognized under the authority of Clement VIII, Urban VIII and Leo XIII; the Propaganda permission of 25 January 1893 says the Glagolitic missal faithfully renders the Roman Missal. Its calendar, now set with Arabic day numbers in place of the Kalends column and without Mass page references, has entries absent from the 1741 printing on 20 October and 14 November and a new first-named feast on 26 November. Institutional scholarship describes a return to Croatian Church Slavonic.
stages.witness_label: Parčić Croatian Church Slavonic restoration witness

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1843 Roman missal and seven-title roster, plus a consignation-of-chalice rite.
Explicitly names the 1843 edition when rejecting three attributed anaphoras, restoring shortened entrance prayers and replacing its constructed Presanctified form.
Confirms exact Latin title, publisher and 1843 imprint.
Original 1843 Propaganda imprint and patriarchal attestation dated Aleppo, 31 August 1840, directly read.
evidence.locus: Latin title PDF 10; attestation and imprimaturs PDF 272

evidence.claim: Original headings establish the seven named anaphora sections; the Presanctified opening explicitly identifies the signing-of-the-chalice service.

Under the heading prayer of the fraction the 1843 common order prints the prayer opening ܗܟܢܐ ܫܪܝܪܐܝܬ ܚܫ ܡܠܬܐ ܐܠܗܐ ܒܒܣܪ (thus truly the Word of God suffered in the flesh), preceded by a long Garshuni rubric; page image read on 2026-10-21.
evidence.locus: Printed 29/PDF 60, centred red heading and following prayer

stages.label: Rome missal with seven named anaphoras
stages.limitations: Original title, attestation and anaphora labels are checked; entrance-prayer restoration and the derivation of the Presanctified compilation remain the 1922 editor’s descriptions. Prayer bodies are not fully transcribed. Shared author labels do not establish textual identity or historical authorship.
stages.reception: Patriarch Ignazio Pietro Giarve attests on 31 August 1840 that the book contains the Syriac missal and rubrics used by Syriac patriarchs, archbishops, bishops and priests in churches and convents. Roman imprimaturs by Dominicus Buttaoni and Joseph Canali appear on the same page. These are the book’s historical attestations; they do not prove uniform later use in every diocese.
stages.scope: Original Catholic celebrant missal with directly checked title, patriarchal attestation and seven anaphora section openings.
stages.summary: The seven named anaphoras are James, Peter, John Chrysostom, Xystus, Matthew the Shepherd, Basil and John Evangelist. Rahmani identifies shortened entrance prayers and a Presanctified compilation constructed from secret prayers of James as features of this 1843 edition.
stages.witness_label: Missale syriacum juxta ritum ecclesiae Antiochenae Syrorum, Rome: Typis S. Congregationis de Propaganda Fide, 1843

evidence.claim: Title gives 1881 imprint; Arabic approval dated 8 September 1880 explicitly identifies Syriac Catholics.
Ordinary supplies minister/congregation text and priest cues; contents show complementary service material.
evidence.locus: PDF 382 printed 7; PDF 375 printed 14; PDF 365–360 printed 24–29; contents PDF 5–13

evidence.claim: Identifies Mosul 1868 Service de la messe privée and its 1881 new edition as an early diaconicon.

stages.label: Mosul deacon and server service book
stages.limitations: A full priest anaphora repertoire is not established by this book. Approval in 1880 is separate from publication in 1881. No whole-missal successor or predecessor relationship to 1922 is inferred.
stages.reception: Arabic approbation expressly addresses Syriac Catholics of Mosul. Its role is auxiliary to celebrant books; the same Eucharistic rite does not make it a new whole-missal state.
stages.scope: Auxiliary Mass-service book: deacon/congregation parts with priest cues, seasonal and departed propers, and pontifical service. Distinct book role from the altar missal.
stages.summary: The ordinary begins with instructions to the deacon and prints deacon/congregation texts around abbreviated priest cues. The Arabic contents distinguish daily service, seasonal/departed propers and pontifical service. Ziadé places the 1868/1881 Mosul Service de la messe line under diaconicon.
stages.witness_label: Ketābā de-tešmeštā de-qurābā be-kullkēn dīlējātā le-fut teksā de-ʿēdtā qaddīštā de-Surjājē; French title Service de la Messe selon le rit syrien avec les prières qui se disent pour les morts, Nouvelle édition, Mossoul: Imprimerie des Pères Dominicains, 1881

evidence.claim: Title names the book of the Mass service according to the Syriac Antiochene rite, compiled by Patriarch Ignatius Ephrem II, printed at the Sharfeh patriarchal press in 1905.

Scope is everything said by deacon, faithful or chanters in simple, solemn or pontifical Mass; the need to reprint led to establishing the text against old manuscripts; Arabic is limited to the Creed, the angels' hymn, the diptychs, the litanies and the Lord's Prayer; a second part of Sunday and feast items is added.

Names six kinds of variable chant and the manuscripts used: one of the eighth and one of the eleventh century, especially the Sharfeh monastery's old codex, and copies used by Aleppo deacons under Patriarch Ignatius Peter.
evidence.locus: PDF 457-452, preface on the second part

evidence.claim: Arabic hymns appended for the fraction in some seasons; the patriarch orders the book followed without deviation.

stages.label: Rahmani's Sharfeh deacon and server book
stages.limitations: Editor-described state; the Syriac body is not collated with the Mosul 1881 book or with the Beirut minister's book that a pencil note on the title page names as a first edition of 1884 (Brightman p. lvi gives a Beirut edition of 1888; that they are one book is not established). The book's predecessor is not identified by the preface, so no transition is drawn.
stages.reception: Prescribed by the Syriac Catholic patriarch for his Church; the order does not prove uniform adoption.
stages.scope: Minister's Mass-service book for deacon, congregation and chanters in simple, solemn and pontifical celebration, with a second part of Sunday and feast chants; distinct book role from the altar missal.
stages.summary: The editor reports a reprinting whose deacon text was established against old manuscripts, kept in Syriac with Arabic only for the Creed, the angels' hymn, the diptychs, the litanies and the Lord's Prayer; a new second part of variable chants for Sundays and feasts compiled from an eighth- and an eleventh-century manuscript, the old Sharfeh codex and copies used by Aleppo deacons; and appended Arabic hymns for the fraction in some seasons. The patriarch orders the book to be kept and followed.
stages.witness_label: Kitab khidmat al-quddas hasab taqs al-kanisa al-suryaniyya al-antakiyya, compiled by Ignatius Ephrem II Rahmani, Sharfeh: Syriac patriarchal press, 1905

evidence.claim: Title identifies edition; James correction and diptych-conclusion removal are explicitly described.
Lists retained/new selection and rejected titles; retains the later six-part diptych arrangement in Twelve Apostles rather than newly introducing it.
Describes fraction, feast/prayer, dismissal, Presanctified and other changes.
Describes Arabic parallel prayers, solemn rubrics, canon-derived admonitions and optional prayers before/after Mass.
Patriarch’s decree dated 8 December 1922 prescribes the edition for his patriarchate and wherever his rite is observed.

Under the red heading prayer of the fraction the formula opens ܠܚܡܐ ܫܡܝܢܐ ܩܨܝܢܢ ܒܫܡܐ ܕܐܒܐ (we break the heavenly bread in the name of the Father), with Amen and a signing cross after each divine name; page image read on 2026-10-21.

The editor cites British Museum Add. 17128 twice: as the older codex in which the Twelve Apostles commemorations of living and dead stand in only two prayers (he follows the later six-part arrangement instead), and as the source of the deprecatory prayers before Communion appended to James.

Identifies Add. 17128 as a 192-leaf vellum sacerdotal of the tenth or eleventh century containing Eucharistic prayers, anaphoras of the Twelve Apostles (fol. 11b), James (fol. 13b), Ignatius, Dionysius, Cyril of Jerusalem and Gregory Nazianzen, and benedictions of the chalice.
evidence.locus: No. CCXC, printed pp. 226–227 (contents p. 226; shelfmark Add. 17,128 at the end of the entry, p. 227)

stages.label: Rahmani’s revised altar missal
stages.limitations: These are primary-described changes, not independent before/after Syriac collation. The editor’s authorship/confessional diagnoses are not adopted as modern critical conclusions. His statement about no alteration to institution narrative/epiclesis is narrower than “no changes to anaphoras.” The six-section Twelve Apostles diptychs are an explicitly retained feature, not a new 1922 innovation. The James manuscript-reference footnote is malformed as printed and needs shelfmark disambiguation.
stages.reception: Issued by Syriac Catholic patriarch Ignatius Ephrem II Rahmani. The decree makes this edition alone authentic within his stated jurisdiction/rite; it does not legislate for all West Syriac churches or prove universal actual adoption.
stages.scope: Revised Syriac Catholic celebrant book with selected anaphoras, ordinary/prayer changes, Presanctified rite, rubrics and Arabic parallel public prayers.
stages.summary: James is revised against older manuscripts and Greek; John Evangelist is followed by Twelve Apostles, Basil of Caesarea, Mark, Eustathius and Cyril of Jerusalem. The editor suppresses Peter/Xystus and rejects three 1843 attributions. He removes conclusions after individual James diptychs; replaces the fraction/consignation formula with “Panem coelestem frangimus”; restores entrance prayers and changes Holy Thursday/Holy Saturday and dismissal prayers. The Presanctified rite is replaced, and solemn-celebration rubrics and preparatory/concluding prayers are added. Arabic is printed beside appropriate Syriac public prayers.
stages.witness_label: Missale iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Apostolicae Antiochenae Syrorum auctoritate recognitum; Ketābā de-taksā de-qūrrābā; Typis Patriarchalibus in Seminario Sciarfensi de Monte Libano, 1922

stages.date_label: September 1930: reported Mass on the day before Benziger's letter of 22 September; context: Holy See decision of 4-5 July 1930

evidence.claim: The liturgical books described as those coming from Propaganda are retained, with non-proper and erroneous expressions to be removed; Kalacherry and Benziger designated to examine them.
Benziger reports receiving Mar Ivanios and Mar Theophilos and states that 'yesterday' (relative to his letter) they said Mass according to the Catholic missal of the Syrian rite of Antioch.

Before reunion Ivanios held printed copies of the missal in use in the Syriac Catholic patriarchate and found it the same as his own except for the commemoration of the pope and the filioque; Patriarch Rahmani wrote from Beirut on 15 January 1928 that he was sending one book of the anaphoras (missal).

stages.label: Reunited bishops celebrate from the Syriac Catholic missal
stages.limitations: The missal used in September 1930 is not identified by edition: it may be a Sharfeh 1922 copy, an earlier Catholic printing or the group's own corrected book. Documents are read in English translation in a documentary edition; Document 52's '29th instant' conflicts with the 20 September 1930 reception date given in Documents 49-51 and 53, so the Mass is dated only as the day before the 22 September letter. The date is an observed use (attestation); the July decision is context, not an effective date of any identified book (cold review 2026-10-22). No textual link to the 1934 Pampakuda book is established.
stages.reception: The earliest reported use by the two reunited bishops; it says nothing about parish practice or about the later printed Malankara books.
stages.scope: Reception event at the 1930 reunion: retention of the liturgical books described as coming from Propaganda, subject to examination, and the bishops' earliest reported Mass according to the Catholic missal of the Syrian rite of Antioch. The missal edition is not identified.
stages.summary: The plenary meeting of the Congregation for the Eastern Church (4 July 1930, approved by Pius XI on 5 July) kept the liturgical books (missals, rituals, pontifical) described as those coming from Propaganda, after removal of improper and erroneous expressions, assigning Bishops Kalacherry and Benziger to examine them. Benziger's report on their reception states that on the previous day Mar Ivanios and Mar Theophilos had said Mass according to the Catholic missal of the Syrian rite of Antioch.
stages.witness_label: Unidentified Catholic missal of the Syrian rite of Antioch named in Bishop Benziger's report of September 1930

evidence.claim: Identifies the Pampakuda 1934 Syro-Malankara missal and names only Xystus and short James.

stages.label: Catholic Pampakuda two-anaphora missal
stages.limitations: Original title, approval, ordinary, anaphoras and Presanctified leaves remain unacquired. Composition dates, identity of short James and direct textual parentage are unestablished. No substantive 1931 → 1934 or 1922 → 1934 transition is established here.
stages.reception: Contemporary source explicitly distinguishes this Syro-Malankara Catholic book from earlier Pampakuda collections. Common West Syriac ancestry alone does not prove Catholic reception of every earlier text.
stages.scope: Source-language Catholic book identified by contemporary bibliography; bounded repertoire state.
stages.summary: Tisserant reports two anaphoras: Xystus and James in its short form. This identifies a different selected repertoire from the 1931 Pampakuda collection and from Rahmani’s 1922 selection, without proving which books furnished its text.
stages.witness_label: Pampakuda Syro-Malankara missal, 1934 (historical bibliographic designation; exact native title not yet inspected)

evidence.claim: Original synodal directions specify voice allocation and posture.
Same report announces a revised Taksa release but does not establish that these directions were already inserted in it.

stages.label: Synodal Holy Qurbono concelebration directions
stages.limitations: Earlier rubrics have not been identified, so this is an attested prescribed rubrical state with no fabricated before/after transition. The 2008 journal date is not the decision date. These directions are separate from the released Taksa's uncollated printing; independent diaspora and lay translation histories remain deferred.
stages.reception: Directions of the Syro-Malankara Catholic synod. Published prescription does not by itself prove adoption rates or exact printing in the released Taksa.
stages.scope: Original 2007 synodal prescription of three Eucharistic concelebration rubrics; distinct from an independently uninspected revised Taksa.
stages.summary: The main celebrant says prayers before the Institution Narrative aloud; concelebrants pronounce the Institution Narrative and chant epiclesis in a low voice; they remain standing during intercessions (Thubden).
stages.witness_label: Fifth Ordinary Holy Episcopal Synod, 9–12 October 2007, Decisions 5.i–iii, published in Malankara Synodal Acts and Voice 3.2 (February 2008), page 40

evidence.claim: The book names Beauvais, episcopal and chapter authority, Paris/Beauvais Fratres Desaint and 1756.
The mandate describes its editorial programme and additional preface categories, is dated 19 April 1756, and commands the book within its named institutions and qualified priest addressees.
evidence.locus: offered images 11–14, complete episcopal mandate; added-preface account image 13; dateline and obligated addressees image 14

evidence.claim: Original calendar, Ordo Missae, Canon and unnotated Advent preface are present at exact inspected loci; no complete wording is imported.
evidence.locus: images 16/24, January/September calendar; image 267 printed p.193; image 303 printed p.229; image 313 printed p.239; image 292 printed p.218

evidence.claim: Original staff notation is present in the end of Præfationes cum cantu and in the Canon ending/Pater. Image 292’s right-column Advent preface is unnotated; the two columns retain different functions.
evidence.locus: Image 292, printed p. 218, left column; image 313, printed p. 239, Canon ending and Pater

stages.label: 1756 Beauvais diocesan missal
stages.limitations: The mandate describes changes relative to earlier practice, but no exact predecessor book has been collated; no substantive transition, native parent, whole-book text or physical completeness is claimed. Publication year and 19 April mandate are distinct events. A later Noyon bibliography (1877) records that 'the old Noyon liturgy' was replaced by the Roman liturgy from Pentecost 1857 by a mandate of Bishop Gignoux; it does not say which books that liturgy used or whether the 1756 Beauvais missal was affected, and no date for the replacement of the Beauvais missal itself has been found.
stages.reception: The mandate directs all churches, chapters, colleges, monasteries and orders of his diocese, and all priests who are bound by law or custom to celebrate or recite the Beauvais Office, to use this missal henceforth. The printed institutional list and qualified priest clause remain distinct. This records the stated command and its recipients, without establishing universal religious-order jurisdiction, uniform actual uptake or a first effective-use date.
stages.scope: The identified 1756 missal with bishop/chapter authority, its scoped mandate, calendar, Mass Order/Canon and prefatory account of selected orations and additional prefaces.
stages.summary: The title names Étienne-René Potier de Gesvres and the cathedral chapter. His mandate, dated 19 April 1756, describes selected orations and additional prefaces for Advent, Corpus Christi, patrons, All Saints and the dead. The mandate directs all churches, chapters, colleges, monasteries and orders of his diocese, and all priests who are bound by law or custom to celebrate or recite the Beauvais Office, to use this missal henceforth. The original calendar, Mass Order/Canon and selected chant notation are directly located.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bellovacense, Fratres Desaint 1756, Lyon SJ L 013/12

stages.date_label: 1750 printing; episcopal letter and mandate dated 17 September 1750

evidence.claim: The title identifies the 1750 Toul printing. The letter dates its mandate 17 September 1750 and names the recipients; its account of changes remains a primary description rather than a collated revision.
evidence.locus: Original title view 11; complete episcopal letter views 13–17, mandate and dateline view 17

evidence.claim: Inspected opening/end/cutoff and following context pages locate the original Ordinarium and strict Canon extents. The wider printed Canon heading continues after the strict prayer; inspection of all interior pages is not claimed.
evidence.locus: Ordinarium opening/end/cutoff views 304/310/311 (located printed pp. 244–250); strict Canon boundary/context views 387/394/395 (located pp. 327–334)

stages.label: 1750 Toul missal
stages.limitations: One publication state is shown. No independent predecessor, exact changed reading, substantive transition, complete text or effective-use date is established. Source view numbers and printed pagination remain distinct.
stages.reception: The mandate names diocesan churches and their deans/rectors, monasteries, colleges, orders, sodalities and communities, followed by priests bound by law or custom to celebrate or recite the Toul Office. The full reach of that qualified priest clause is unresolved; universal territorial application or actual compliance is not established.
stages.scope: An identified 1750 Toul missal, its title and scoped episcopal mandate, and selected original Mass Order and Canon loci.
stages.summary: The original title prints 1750. Scipion-Jérôme Bégon’s letter, dated 17 September 1750, describes changes to collects, prefaces, readings and other propers and orders the book within its named recipients. Its legal scope and the printing year are distinct from an observed first-use date.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum cathedralis ecclesiae et dioecesis Tullensis (Toul, 1750), Lyon SJ L 013/7

evidence.claim: The original identifies Tournai use and the Paris 20 October 1498 printing event.
evidence.locus: Source PP 5, title; PP 21, temporal incipit; PP 582, colophon

evidence.claim: Selected original divisions and Mass material are located. Strict Canon ends at final Per omnia/Amen before Pater on PP 310; the printed Canon heading continues through PP 312. The Creed and preparation material support a bounded Ordinary component, without a complete Ordinary claim.
evidence.locus: Source PP 7/18, calendar; PP 19, Accidentia; PP 299, preface and Creed; PP 307/310, strict Canon boundaries, with following context PP 311/312; PP 313, Common; PP 351, Sanctoral; PP 579, preparation

stages.label: 1498 Tournai missal
stages.limitations: One printing attests a book state. No full transcription, physical completeness, distinct substantive recension, predecessor, adoption date or ancestry is established.
stages.reception: The book’s own title and incipit declare Tournai use; particular churches’ receipt or use of this exact printing remains unverified.
stages.scope: The Ghent copy of a 1498 Paris missal expressly naming the Tournai church’s use; no separate diocesan reform is identified.
stages.summary: The title and temporal incipit name Tournai use. The original colophon records Paris, Johannes Higman, expenses of Wilhelm Houtmart, and completion on 20 October 1498. The retained offered images support this identified printed witness, without establishing approval or implementation.
stages.witness_label: Missale Tornacense (Paris, Johannes Higman, 1498), Ghent BHSL.RES.1379

evidence.claim: The surviving original identifies Liège use and a 24 November 1499 Paris printing. The expense clause does not alone identify the printer’s workshop.

Canon images show lower text loss. The library reports leaf 1 (a1) missing, 274 (K6) pasted, and text loss at 169 (X1), 177 (X9), 178 (X10), 180 (X12); its folio conventions are distinct from modern pencil and IIIF labels.
evidence.locus: IIIF canvases 361–366, Canon; BSB copy record M-437,1

evidence.claim: Other copies of the same edition preserve leaf a1 as a title leaf with a printed description of the book, followed by a movable-feast table, and confirm the 24 November 1499 Higman colophon.
evidence.locus: XV.B200 PDF 6–8 (a1r title, a1v tabula, a ii calendar) and PDF 540 colophon

stages.label: 1499 Liège missal
stages.limitations: Copy defects prevent a complete-text or complete-Canon claim. The 1499 date is a printing event, not approval or actual local receipt. No substantive revision, exact predecessor or ancestry follows from the incipit or colophon. The BSB copy record reports leaf a1 missing; ULiège copies XV.B200 and XV.A46 show a title leaf and movable-feast table at that position, which is other-copy evidence only.
stages.reception: The surviving book declares Liège use; present BSB holding is not evidence of historical use there, and receipt by any particular Liège church is unestablished.
stages.scope: A physically defective surviving 1499 Liège-use missal copy, with original local-use incipit and printing colophon directly inspected.
stages.summary: The surviving incipit names the Liège church’s use. The colophon records Paris, publication at Johannes Higman’s expense, and 24 November 1499. The library copy catalogue reports first leaf a1 missing, and the surviving images have visible losses; those defects remain part of the witness.
stages.witness_label: Missale Leodiense (Paris,1499), BSB 2 Inc.c.a.3785 / bsb 00075725

evidence.claim: Liège use, emendation and added-office claims; Paris 22 July 1540; sold at Liège by Olivier Boulongne.
Four appended Masses; 21 November Columbanus.
evidence.locus: PDF 605–611 appended Masses; PDF 612 register; PDF 20 calendar

evidence.claim: The 1499 edition also has Columbanus on 21 November and no Presentation entry.

stages.label: 1540 Liège missal (Paris, July issue)
stages.limitations: The 1499 sanctoral was not searched for these Masses and the intervening Liège editions (1500–1527, March 1540) are unchecked, so no 1499 → 1540 transition is asserted. Identity with catalogue lead amiet-nonfrance-liege-1540-7223 (USTC 438087) is unresolved because BnF records two 1540 issues.
stages.reception: A Liège bookseller and later Liège Jesuit ownership are attested; use in any particular church is not.
stages.scope: A 1540 Liège-use missal copy with original title, imprint, November calendar, appended Masses and register inspected.
stages.summary: The title says the book was newly purged of errors and adds offices hitherto wanting, listed at the end; four Masses (Seven Sorrows, recollection of the Marian feasts, Presentation of Mary, Holy Tear) are appended before the register. The November calendar keeps Columbanus on 21 November without a Presentation entry, as in the ULiège 1499 copy XV.B200.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Leodiensis, Paris 22 July 1540, ULiège R00424D

evidence.claim: The original identifies Tarazona use and a 13 February 1500 Pamplona printing commissioned by the bishop and chapter; selected Mass material is present.
evidence.locus: PDF p. 14, local-use instruction; p. 19, temporal incipit; p. 329, Mass preparation; p. 656, colophon

evidence.claim: The library reports two missing leaves of the first gathering, the whole gathering signed Z, leaf C-6 and one leaf of the third-numeration gathering D; this is a library condition report, not a new physical collation.
evidence.locus: Modern holding-library copy-description card, PDF p. 1

stages.label: 1500 Tarazona missal
stages.limitations: Only the six named images were directly inspected. No complete Ordinary or Canon, native transcription, exact predecessor state, distinct recension or substantive revision is established. The 1529 printing/copy cluster remains separate and uncollated.
stages.reception: The incipit and instruction declare Tarazona use and the colophon names local commissioning; these do not prove receipt or compliance by all diocesan churches.
stages.scope: A physically defective 1500 Tarazona-use missal, with original use-instruction, temporal incipit, Mass-preparation material and printing/commissioning colophon inspected.
stages.summary: The original incipit identifies a mixed missal for Tarazona church and diocese. Its colophon names Pamplona, printer Arnaldus Guillermus de Broquario and completion on 13 February 1500, and attributes commissioning to Bishop Guillermus Raymundus de Moncada with the dean and chapter. The book’s local commissioning statement does not supply a separate promulgation or observed implementation.
stages.witness_label: Missale mixtum secundum usum ecclesie et diocesis Tirasonensis (Pamplona,Brocar,1500), Bizkaia INC-35

stages.date_label: 1 June 1488 printing reported by Lambert; original book unacquired

evidence.claim: The scholarly copy report identifies the 1488 local book and its described replacements, retained Holy Saturday supplication and defective-tail limit. The reported 1 June 1488 date is a printing event, not a directly inspected episcopal act or uptake date.
evidence.locus: Lambert section VII, printed p. 42 heading and pp. 42–43 reported colophon and copy description; retained article PDF pp. 20–21

stages.label: 1488 Huesca missal described by Lambert
stages.limitations: The stage documents only a scholarly-described printed witness. No original wording, full textual state, physical completeness, independent recension, revision edge or native parent is established. A possible appended supplement remains unresolved, rather than absent.
stages.reception: The scholar identifies the local Huesca book; no directly inspected episcopal mandate or actual parish receipt is established here.
stages.scope: The 1488 Huesca missal as described by Lambert’s inspected scholarly copy report, including his explicit defective-tail limit.
stages.summary: Lambert reports a 1488 Huesca adaptation of 1485 Zaragoza sheets with a local calendar, bishop letter, colophon and pasted heading. He reports retention of an archbishop supplication in Holy Saturday and says his copy’s lost tail prevents deciding whether a local saints supplement followed. These are attributed copy descriptions; the original 1488 book remains unacquired.
stages.witness_label: Lambert, Notes sur divers incunables d’Aragon (1910), section VII on the 1488 Missale Oscense

stages.date_label: 1504 printing (catalogue-reported year; title and colophon uninspected)

evidence.claim: A 1504 Zaragoza printing for the use of the churches of Huesca and Jaca is catalogued with two Barbastro copies.
evidence.locus: USTC edition 347646, title, imprint, copies and references

stages.label: 1504 missal for the churches of Huesca and Jaca, Zaragoza (Coci)
stages.limitations: Provisional because the evidence is catalogue metadata only: no original image, mandate or colophon has been inspected, so the date stays catalogue-reported and the Huesca–Jaca use is taken from the recorded title. Components are those implied by a complete missal title, not observed. No relation to the 1488 book or to Zaragoza books is claimed.
stages.reception: The title names Huesca and Jaca; no dated local use is established.
stages.scope: One catalogued printed missal whose recorded title names the use of the churches of Huesca (Osca) and Jaca.
stages.summary: USTC records a folio Latin missal 'secundum ritum insignium ecclesiarum Oscensis et Iaccensi, admodum completum', printed at Zaragoza by Jorge Coci in 1504, under the heading Missale – Huesca; USUARIUM 7335 carries the same title and year.
stages.witness_label: Copies recorded at Barbastro cathedral (USTC 347646); no digitisation located

stages.date_label: 1485 printing, original Salins colophon; mandate notice undated

evidence.claim: The original notice states its Besançon-customary and episcopal commissioning claim; the colophon identifies a Salins printing in 1485. The notice’s mandate is not independently dated.
evidence.locus: Viewer image 267, printer notice; image 606, final red colophon

evidence.claim: The named original leaves locate calendar and Mass divisions, without a complete Ordinary or Canon transcription.
evidence.locus: Images 4–15, calendar; 393–399, preparation, Ordo and prefaces; 401–403, common preface and Canon; 403–406, Pater, later rites and thanksgiving; 407, Annunciation

evidence.claim: The catalogue supplies the conventional book title and reports the missing final blank. The 606 descriptions are the offered enumeration, not a full acquired facsimile.
evidence.locus: Holding-library conventional title, INC.98 shelfmark and copy-condition note; complete offered description sequence

stages.label: 1485 Besançon missal printed at Salins
stages.limitations: The first three inspected opening frames do not supply a conventional printed title leaf. Forty selected images and a library report of the missing final blank do not certify physical completeness. No whole-book text, independent predecessor comparison, distinct recension, substantive transition or historical parentage is established.
stages.reception: The original printer notice asserts an episcopal mandate for the Besançon customary. It supplies neither a separately dated act nor evidence of receipt or actual use by a particular cathedral, monastery or parish.
stages.scope: The 1485 Salins missal witness, its printed Besançon-customary commissioning notice, and selected original calendar and Mass divisions; no separate dated approval state.
stages.summary: The original final colophon gives Salins and 1485. A separate printed notice names Jean Des Prés, Benoît Bigot and Claude Bodram and states the express mandate of Caroli de Novocastro for the Besançon customary. No separately located or dated commissioning act is supplied. Selected original Mass Order, Canon and other divisions attest this bounded local book witness.
stages.witness_label: Besançon INC.98, catalogued Missale Bisuntinense (Salins, 1485)

traditions.scope: Particular Mass propers of the Diocese of Würzburg as adjuncts to the postconciliar Roman Missal, kept separate from any medieval or early-modern local use of the same see.

traditions.scope: Proper calendars of the Austrian dioceses, including Salzburg, Gurk and Graz-Seckau, as adjuncts to the postconciliar Roman books.

traditions.coverage_note: Exact Greek receiving altar books remain unknown. A distinct Greek–Albanian Roma 1967 setting now has directly inspected title, generic undated Holy See approval leaf and 15 December 1967 S. Nilo printing colophon. Its identity with reported 1968 printings, other reported bilingual formats and particular Lungro receiving copies remains unestablished; the original dated approval/adoption decree remains unacquired.
traditions.label: Eparchy of Lungro: received liturgical language and local Ordo
traditions.scope: A named approved Arbëresh Chrysostom Liturgy with reported parish use; the 2026 local annual Ordo.

traditions.coverage_note: A local calendar/rubric witness does not identify a full celebrant book or prove first/uniform adoption.
traditions.label: Eparchy of Piana: local calendar and rubric reference books
traditions.scope: The 2019 eparchial Imerologhion and its explicit Greek/Italian Anthologion reference sets.

traditions.coverage_note: Published planned arrangements are distinguished from completed celebration and exact service-book reception.
traditions.label: Athens Greek Catholic cathedral: announced 2026 service calendar
traditions.scope: The Holy Trinity cathedral/parish Holy Week programme; no claim about all Greek exarchate communities.

traditions.coverage_note: The books have explicit local private-use publishing permission and separately evidenced operative reception. The dossier does not equate private permission with general public-language authorization or establish a seventeenth-century-to-present chain.
traditions.label: Hungarian Greek Catholic Hajdúdorog received service books
traditions.scope: The 1920 revised combined Liturgikon and its 1949 Chrysostom extract, in Hungarian with Greek canonical parts in the full book.

traditions.coverage_note: Two inspected printings and one bounded calendar change; the defective 1485 copy, 1531/1540/1552/1598 printings, Roman adoption and local reception remain open.
traditions.label: Zaragoza (Caesaraugustan) local missal
traditions.scope: Printed Missale Caesaraugustanum states whose original title, holy-day list and colophon leaves were inspected.

traditions.coverage_note: Two inspected printings and one bounded calendar change; the 1492 incunable, later printings, Roman adoption and reception remain open.
traditions.label: Valencia local missal
traditions.scope: Printed Missale Valentinum states whose original title, January calendar and colophon leaves were inspected.

traditions.coverage_note: One documented 1499 publication state resting on scholarly description and catalogue contents, not on an inspected original leaf (the BVPB copy refused access with HTTP 429 on 21 and 22 October 2026). The c. 1396 Reus manuscript, the 1550 Lyon printing, archiepiscopal authority and Roman adoption remain open.
traditions.label: Tarragona local missal
traditions.scope: Tarragona missal editions: the 1499 Rosembach printing as described with exact loci by Altés i Aguiló (2011) and catalogued by USUARIUM; no original leaf inspected by this lane.

traditions.coverage_note: Two documented publication states; no original leaf of either printing was inspected directly except the 1535–1536 title page reproduced in Pallarés Jiménez (2015). No transition between them is documented: the 1535 contract and Altés describe correction of the texts but name no changed formulary.
traditions.label: Urgell local missal
traditions.scope: Urgell missal editions of 1509 (Venice) and 1535–1536 (Zaragoza, Coci), documented through scholarly descriptions with exact loci, a reproduced title page and a transcribed 1535 printing contract; manuscript missals and the 1557 Lyon printing remain catalogue witnesses.

traditions.coverage_note: Original leaves of four printings and their relations remain incompletely collated.
traditions.label: Aquileian local Mass books
traditions.scope: The Aquileian church missal printings; individual edition identities, not a continuous normalized text.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1617 book is indexed with a bishop’s decree and Ordinary; the decree and comparison with 1733 remain uninspected.
traditions.label: Aosta diocesan Mass books
traditions.scope: Local Missale Augustense printings for Aosta, distinct from Augsburg.

traditions.coverage_note: Dates and holdings are bounded; no full recension, use history or manuscript collation is proved.
traditions.label: Benevento missal manuscripts
traditions.scope: Two separately shelfmarked Benevento missals, with scribal style and present or former holding distinguished from local liturgical authority.

traditions.coverage_note: Only the identified copies and the 1499 contents are mapped; no print-to-print revisions or adoption dates are established.
traditions.label: Messina local Missal printings
traditions.scope: Edition-identified Missale Messanense books in the examined catalogue.

traditions.coverage_note: No candidate in the existing Western coverage row identifies a Padua local Mass recension.
traditions.label: Padua Mass-book leads
traditions.scope: Padua-origin and Padua-held books requiring specific Mass text and use attribution.

traditions.coverage_note: A bounded local annual ceremonial order is admitted from H14, with a documented 1101–1300 attestation in monza-local-next.json; its ff. 47–74 do not supply a complete Missal or Ordinary. F.1/101 and Berengar treasury 98/89 remain separately identified holdings without established Monza liturgical use. Full original texts, reception and sequence remain open.
traditions.label: Monza Mass-book leads
traditions.scope: Monza-related sacramentary, chant and order-book records requiring provenance and Mass-use tests.

traditions.coverage_note: No complete Ravenna Missal or independently dated local recension is identified in the reviewed set.
traditions.label: Ravenna Mass-book leads
traditions.scope: Ravenna-attributed components and fragments requiring physical identification and use context.

traditions.coverage_note: Page-collated states 1550, 1553, 1603 and 1604 bracket the Suscepimus Deus recombination. The 1985 postconciliar Proprium (Missal and Lectionary) is documented from its front matter as a supplement to the Roman Missal, which the Order was permitted to assume on 2 June 1969; the preconciliar 1933–1965 missals and the 1604–1985 interval are not staged.
traditions.label: Dominican use
traditions.scope: Latin missals of the Order of Preachers; the selected original Latin printings, not a translation history.

traditions.coverage_note: Two printings establish a bounded October calendar change. The precise intervening act is not yet identified. A confirmed 1972 general-council decree adopting the postconciliar Roman Missal (with a personal exception for older friars) marks the Order's change of book; it is an adoption event, not a stage.
traditions.label: Carmelite use
traditions.scope: Latin missals of the ancient observance of the Order of Carmel; not the Discalced Carmelites’ separate Roman-use books.

traditions.coverage_note: 1538–1558 change is established through original scholarship. The 1924 approved state has direct prefatory evidence; its precise body revision remains open.
traditions.label: Rite of Braga
traditions.scope: Bracarense Latin missals, kept distinct from Roman, Carmelite and Dominican uses.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1582 preparation and 1603 Gloria are reported through page-checked scholarship; the 1627 title and three Ordinary pages are directly image-checked. No complete-book reconstruction is asserted. An undated incunable missal (BSB-Ink [1496]; GW not after 1496) is recorded as a provisional stage; it prints the same oblation prayer, with word-order variants, and the same Gloria reading as 1561.
traditions.label: Carthusian use
traditions.scope: Carthusian Latin missals and the complementary Ordinarium; chapter and publication dates are distinguished.

traditions.coverage_note: Two manuscript states are distinguished without making their differences a single linear reform.
traditions.label: Sarum use
traditions.scope: Selected medieval Sarum missal witnesses, read through Legg’s critical edition.

traditions.coverage_note: Local manuscript features and printed differences are documented; a diocesan revision mechanism is not established.
traditions.label: Hereford use
traditions.scope: The Whitchurch manuscript and the 1502 Hereford printing, through Henderson’s edition.

traditions.coverage_note: Five printed witnesses are not five demonstrated recensions.
traditions.label: York use
traditions.scope: The early printed York sequence as compared by Henderson, with manuscript diversity retained as a limitation.

traditions.coverage_note: Substantive repertory differences are established by scholarship; the exact sequence of intermediate revisions is not.
traditions.label: Esztergom use
traditions.scope: The pre-1341 notated missal and 1484 Esztergom printing as compared in Déri’s critical edition.

traditions.coverage_note: 1774/1775 complementary books, a named 1845 exemplar, 1906 and 1946 editorial states, and the 1955–1962 restoration are distinguished. No continuous textual stemma is claimed.
traditions.label: Syro-Malabar Eucharistic books
traditions.scope: Syro-Malabar Syriac and approved operative Malayalam Eucharistic service-book language, with Latin restoration instruments and bounded reception; independent diaspora and lay translation histories are deferred.

traditions.coverage_note: First printing through 2005 with a bounded manuscript precursor and 2003-2006 synodal reception prescriptions. Dates mark attestation/publication/approval, not continuous use. The 2005 stage now rests on the original Arabic decree and introductions read in the 2005 people's volume (Kitab al-Mu'minin); the celebrant's bilingual Syriac/Arabic volumes remain unseen. The 1816 Qozhaya and 1959 states rest on Boutros Gemayel's 1970 description of the printed editions, read on page images; Gemayel also supplies the full 1716 roster beside Dib, Kaufhold, Feulner and the 2005 presentation. The 1959 state is an unofficial practical edition.
traditions.label: Maronite Antiochene Qurbono
traditions.scope: Maronite Eucharistic books in Syriac and native Syriac/Arabic composition; independent vernacular translation history excluded.

traditions.coverage_note: One bounded order-book state; no complete Mass text, continuous sequence, or whole-book recension is reconstructed.
traditions.label: Monza local Roman ceremonial order
traditions.scope: The local annual order of San Giovanni Battista in Monza attested by H14, distinguished from Monza-held sacramentaries and Ambrosian books.

traditions.coverage_note: The British Library witness is fragmentary and composite. Its geographic origin does not by itself establish a recension or ancestry for the printed missal.
traditions.label: Old Hispanic manuscript witnesses; recension unassigned
traditions.scope: Identified medieval witnesses whose exact A/B classification has not been established in this dossier.

traditions.coverage_note: Distinct from B, especially in reading arrangements and parts of the Mass structure. No individually collated A manuscript stage is yet admitted here. The Praenotanda attribution to Julian of Toledo is an historical hypothesis, not an independently dated stage.
traditions.label: Hispanic manuscript tradition A
traditions.scope: The manuscript tradition represented, in the 1988 Praenotanda, by most northern witnesses and the Santa Eulalia scriptorium at Toledo.

traditions.coverage_note: B is not a corrupt form of A. The 1500 compilation transmits B through editorial work and Roman devotional additions; many manuscript exemplars used by its editors are lost. The print is not an intact seventh-century missal.
traditions.label: Tradition B and its Toledan printed transmission
traditions.scope: The Saints Justa and Rufina manuscript tradition as represented through the 1500 printed compilation and its later editions.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1991 Temporal and 1994 complementary volume form one missal corpus. Approval dates, separate Order volumes and Liber Commicus publications do not create successive replacements of the whole missal.
traditions.label: Modern Hispano-Mozarabic critical corpus
traditions.scope: Modern missal and complementary lectionary assembled from both manuscript traditions for Catholic Hispano-Mozarabic worship.

traditions.coverage_note: The edited print and its foreword establish the book and intended scope, but do not establish uniform local reception or a collated transition from earlier Nidaros books.
traditions.label: Nidaros provincial missal
traditions.scope: The printed 1519 Nidaros-use missal commissioned for the metropolitan province; Iceland and the Faroes are within the stated intended territory.

traditions.coverage_note: The National Library describes a composite parchment copy; print date and local components are identified, but original leaves and other copies are uncollated.
traditions.label: Turku diocesan Missale Aboense
traditions.scope: The 1488 Lübeck-printed Missale Aboense and its diocesan preface and calendar.

traditions.coverage_note: The title and contents are transcribed in a scholarly catalogue. The original synod act, exact effective date, and later Zagreb cathedral and Jesuit routes are unresolved.
traditions.label: Zagreb diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Venetian 1511 Missale Zagrabiense bearing a title that reports diocesan synod and chapter approval under Bishop Luke.

traditions.coverage_note: A digitized-book title transcription identifies the edition. Papal concession documents, original title image, complete propers, and reception remain uninspected. This is not assigned as a successor to the medieval Prague-use core.
traditions.label: Roman-Bohemian missal
traditions.scope: The 1690 Roman-based missal printed at the Prague archiepiscopal seminary with Bohemian saints' proper Masses named on its title.

traditions.coverage_note: Mandate, title, colophon and January calendars are inspected in BSB copies; Mass bodies, other months and local reception remain uncollated.
traditions.label: Halberstadt diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed missals for the diocese of Halberstadt issued under Archbishop Ernst of Magdeburg as administrator: the c. 1498 edition with his mandate and the 1511 edition.

traditions.coverage_note: No original copy was located online; catalogue witness only.
traditions.label: Lübeck diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Missale Lubicense catalogued for about 1505.

traditions.coverage_note: No original copy was located online; catalogue witness only.
traditions.label: Merseburg diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Missale Merseburgense catalogued for 1502.

traditions.coverage_note: One locally commissioned manuscript is identified; its relation to other English uses is not collated.
traditions.label: Westminster Abbey missal
traditions.scope: The Abbey's Litlyngton manuscript for its High Altar, not a general English diocesan rite.

traditions.coverage_note: A dated manuscript is known; the calendar and Mass texts need direct collation.
traditions.label: Arbuthnott and St Andrews manuscript use
traditions.scope: The Arbuthnott manuscript witness associated with St Andrews; not every St Andrews church.

traditions.coverage_note: The library identifies Irish Carmelite use; manuscript layers and textual relation to other Carmelite books are uncollated.
traditions.label: Kilcormac Carmelite Mass witness
traditions.scope: The Mass-book portion of Trinity College Dublin MS 82, distinguished from its separate antiphonal portion.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1626 title and BnF copy establish a bounded book; distribution and use by particular priests are unknown.
traditions.label: English, Scottish and Irish itinerant mission book
traditions.scope: Small Roman-derived Mass and ritual print intended for travelling priests in the named territories.

traditions.label: Odense missal print witnesses
traditions.scope: Identified 1483 and 1501 Odense printings, each with fragmentary survivors.

traditions.coverage_note: The holding library identifies one printing and copy; earlier printed-book relations remain uncollated.
traditions.label: Copenhagen Missale Hafniense witness
traditions.scope: The 1510 Copenhagen print, without an inferred separate diocesan rite.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1522 item is a component book, not a complete annual missal or a documented revision of the c.1484 edition.
traditions.label: Roskilde Mass-book witnesses
traditions.scope: The c.1484 missal and a separate 1522 Canon with selected Masses and Common.

traditions.coverage_note: The exact Riga copy and its body text have not been inspected directly.
traditions.label: Viborg missal print
traditions.scope: The 1500 Liber missalis catalogued for Viborg.

traditions.coverage_note: Three identified Copenhagen copies belong to one printing, not three text states; no 1512 edition is established.
traditions.label: Schleswig Missale Slesvicense
traditions.scope: The 1486 Schleswig-use missal printed by Stephan Arndes.

traditions.coverage_note: Production in Iceland or Norway is unresolved; the five leaves do not establish a complete local recension.
traditions.label: Icelandic Nidaros-use breviary-missal
traditions.scope: Five surviving leaves of a small Mass and Office manuscript associated with Iceland and Nidaros use.

traditions.label: Skarð missal manuscript
traditions.scope: Surviving leaves of Missale Scardense, AM Acc. 7 Hs 1 with identified dispersed fragments.

traditions.coverage_note: This Mass-chant book is separate from Missale Scardense and does not attest a complete missal text.
traditions.label: Gufudal Mass gradual manuscript
traditions.scope: Surviving chant leaves of Graduale Gufudalense, AM Acc. 7 Hs 2 and identified dispersed leaves.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1570 reuse is a provenance event, not a Mass-use date; Bergen reception remains attributed, not proven.
traditions.label: Nordfjord and probable Bergen reception witness
traditions.scope: One French-origin Mass leaf reused in a 1570 Nordfjord diploma, with possible earlier Bergen-area use.

traditions.coverage_note: No diocese, source codex extent or recension is established.
traditions.label: Unassigned Danish notated missal fragment
traditions.scope: RA 4613, catalogued as a Danish notated missal fragment.

traditions.coverage_note: Municipal library identifies a 1150s manuscript and cathedral use; import from England is reported as a belief, not proven textual ancestry.
traditions.label: Skara cathedral missal witness
traditions.scope: Missale Scarense manuscript in the Skara diocesan and cathedral setting.

traditions.coverage_note: The holding catalogue maps calendar, temporal, Ordinary/Canon and fragmentary sanctoral; no complete text or exact copying year follows.
traditions.label: Linköping secular missal witness
traditions.scope: National Library of Sweden A 97, two-unit local Mass manuscript with losses.

traditions.coverage_note: One exact copy and print are identified; original leaves and local revision history are uncollated.
traditions.label: Strängnäs missal print
traditions.scope: The 1487 Ghotan printed Missale Strengnense.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1946 facsimile is a modern delivery witness, not a 1946 liturgical state.
traditions.label: Lund missal print
traditions.scope: The 1514 Hopyl printed Missale Lundense.

traditions.coverage_note: Its relation to the earlier Uppsala print is not claimed without direct compared loci.
traditions.label: Uppsala missal print
traditions.scope: The 1513 Basel printing according to Uppsala church rite.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1896 Rule edition is a modern textual witness, not the manuscript copying date.
traditions.label: St Augustine's Abbey Canterbury missal
traditions.scope: Corpus Christi College Cambridge MS 270, a manuscript Mass book for the Canterbury abbey.

traditions.coverage_note: A local St Thomas inscription is evidence of association; exact use throughout Dublin is not established.
traditions.label: Dublin associated Mass manuscript
traditions.scope: British Library Add. MS 24198, with Mass and other ceremonial material including an abbot blessing.

traditions.coverage_note: It is not established that the two leaves came from one codex; a 1519 Aarhus breviary is an Office book, not a second Mass-book witness.
traditions.label: Aarhus Cathedral Mass-book leaves
traditions.scope: Two surviving late-medieval notated leaves found reused in the cathedral pulpit.

traditions.coverage_note: The official 1975 notice confirms OCSO prayers and reading indications; the shared Ritual identifies a Rome 1983 proper whose OCist publication and 1977 confirmation are independently attested. The overview's general 1983 approval report remains discrepant. No whole OCSO Missal, continuous use, inherited text or medieval OCSO identity is established.
traditions.label: Cistercians of the Strict Observance (OCSO)
traditions.scope: Postconciliar Latin Mass-proper components and their relation to the Roman Missal base, the OCist branch, and named house reception.

traditions.coverage_note: The early printing has conflicting bibliographic and colophon years; the directly seen 1926 book is a proper of Mass and Office. Neither supplies a continuous OSA missal sequence.
traditions.label: Augustinian Hermits (OSA)
traditions.scope: Order-labelled Latin missal and Mass proper witnesses, distinct from Augustinian Canons Regular and Recollect translations.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1560 Barcelona missal is an incomplete surviving copy, while the 1976 approval concerns only a proper. Intervening witnesses and text are not collated.
traditions.label: Order of Mercy (Mercedarians)
traditions.scope: Mercedarian whole-missal bibliography and a separately approved Latin Mass proper.

traditions.coverage_note: The medieval codex is Roman Curia use for Servite friars. Its additions and the 1998 second typical edition need original-page review.
traditions.label: Servite Order
traditions.scope: The medieval Servite-use manuscript and the two complementary 1972 Latin Mass-proper volumes.

traditions.coverage_note: The manuscript Mass folios and 1529 printing remain uninspected; the 1975 official approval establishes a proper, not a complete missal.
traditions.label: Order of the Most Holy Trinity (Trinitarians)
traditions.scope: Mixed medieval Mass-book witness, a catalogued printed missal, and an approved modern proper, with their different evidence classes preserved.

traditions.coverage_note: The owning BnF catalogue rejects the former 1551 date for its B-320 copy. The medieval local books and later 2005 proper remain without a checked original-text sequence.
traditions.label: Hospitaller Order of Saint John of Jerusalem, Rhodes and Malta
traditions.scope: A corrected 1553 printed-missal catalogue identity and the 1987 Latin proper with lectionary.

traditions.coverage_note: Two bounded manuscript states supported by inspected studies and official descriptions; original full manuscripts, complete texts, revisions and adoption remain open.
traditions.label: Padua cathedral rubrics and Mass-book witnesses
traditions.scope: Named Eucharistic rubrics in local cathedral ordinal E.57 and identified chant loci of Roman Missal D.30; the books do not define a continuous independent Padua recension.

traditions.coverage_note: None establishes a Ravenna annual Missal, continuous local use, a complete Eucharistic prayer, or a textual transition. Independent dates and origin qualifications control each witness.
traditions.label: Mass-book fragments attributed to Ravenna: local use unproved
traditions.scope: Four physically identified fragmentary Eucharistic-book states associated with Ravenna in scholarship or origin catalogues, including northern Italian lectionary strips whose Ravenna use is unproved. A research grouping, not one local recension or lineage.

traditions.coverage_note: The title names three substitutive components under Apostolic See authority; exact prayers, rubrics, donor printing, and 1864 permission terms remain uncollated.
traditions.label: Roman–Lyonese missal
traditions.scope: The 1866 Latin Romano-Lyonese missal and its expressly named local substitutions; no continuous descent from earlier Lyon-use books is asserted.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1986 book is contemporary-described after separate 1983 approval and 1984 Roman confirmation; later expanded printings are retrospective descriptions pending original leaves.
traditions.label: Roman Missal for the dioceses of Poland
traditions.scope: Approved Polish-language diocesan service books and their regional calendar and Eucharistic components, distinct from the Latin typical edition and older Polish local uses.

traditions.coverage_note: The people's book itself gives 2007 promulgation and required-use dates; 1964/65, Parma 1970, and Passaic 1996 predecessors are not collapsed into one text.
traditions.label: Pittsburgh Byzantine Catholic Divine Liturgies
traditions.scope: The Metropolia of Pittsburgh's English Chrysostom and Basil service set for four eparchies, with the acquired 2006 people's book distinguished from two unacquired clergy Liturgikons.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1988 official decree and selected order and prayer excerpts are inspected; a complete approved bound missal and its publication and effective-use dates are not.
traditions.label: Roman Missal for the dioceses of Zaire
traditions.scope: French original-language Roman adaptation approved for the dioceses of then-Zaire, not an Africa-wide recension.

traditions.coverage_note: The bishops' official account identifies the book, approval month, use date, and bounded components; the original approval leaf and 2003-to-2015 collation are outstanding.
traditions.label: Divine Worship: The Missal for the personal ordinariates
traditions.scope: The 2015 Prayer Book English Roman Rite missal approved for the three personal ordinariates, distinct from the 2014 non-Eucharistic Occasional Services.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1493 and 1733 catalogue duplicates are not extra editions. The 1717 title claims General Chapter authority, but the underlying act and the 1717–1733 component changes are unverified.
traditions.label: Cluniac use
traditions.scope: Four individually identified printed Cluniac missals, kept apart from the undated history of their texts and reception.

traditions.coverage_note: The manuscript's copying range and the printed book's publication date do not establish a revision or direct descent.
traditions.label: Humiliati use
traditions.scope: One fifteenth-century manuscript and one 1504 printed whole missal identified in USUARIUM.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1569 Manuale has unverified Mass content and is not represented as a missal; the 1976 notice is an approval, not a dated publication or observed use.
traditions.label: Order of Minims
traditions.scope: A catalogued eighteenth-century Mass proper and the Holy See's 1976 approval of Latin and Italian Mass and Office propers.

traditions.coverage_note: 1925, 1950 and 1959 are proper witnesses, not whole missals. Their Mass texts are uncollated; the 2025 printed Latin decree controls its dates and scoped local calendar grades.
traditions.label: Discalced Carmelites (OCD)
traditions.scope: Individually dated Latin Mass proper books and the order's 2025 second typical edition with its complementary lectionary.

traditions.coverage_note: The 1536 authorization request and 1541 inventory do not date the first printing. The 1560 catalogue date does not itself establish a distinct rite or a third-edition text history.
traditions.label: Military Order of Santiago
traditions.scope: The identified 1560 order missal only; earlier print reports, an unverified manuscript and an evangeliary are kept as gaps or contextual components.

traditions.coverage_note: The extant copy is fragmentary and original pages have not been independently collated here.
traditions.label: Barcelona local Mass books
traditions.scope: The identified 1498 Barcelona Missal and its surviving fragment, not a complete diocesan recension.

traditions.coverage_note: Its title reports correction and augmentation, but the relevant predecessor and decree remain uninspected.
traditions.label: Salamanca local Mass books
traditions.scope: The 1533 Missale Salmanticense as an identified local printed book.

traditions.coverage_note: The printer's correction claim is not a component-level comparison or a normative decree.
traditions.label: Seville local Mass books
traditions.scope: The identified 1565 Missale Hispalense, including its inspected title and printer's preface.

traditions.coverage_note: Its title describes additions; original pages and predecessor comparison are uninspected.
traditions.label: Toledo Roman-type local Mass books
traditions.scope: The identified 1551 Roman-type Toledo Missal, kept separate from the Hispano-Mozarabic books.

traditions.coverage_note: A local title and component inventory do not establish an ancient Gallican ancestry or a complete textual state.
traditions.label: Cosenza local Mass books
traditions.scope: The catalogue-identified Missale Cosentinum of 1549 and its indexed Mass components.

traditions.coverage_note: The English translation's independent history and any claim of an altar-book recension are outside this stage.

transitions.limitations: Text-collated applies to three complete prayer units, their local rubrics, and the Holy Saturday ending on the identified pages. The Holy Saturday quotations are bounded excerpts, not complete service transcriptions. Wider calendar, lectionary, and chant changes have primary-description evidence and have not been exhaustively collated. This is an institutional Cistercian revision relation, not proof that the 1657 typesetter directly copied this particular 1606 edition. All six complete prayer bodies have passed independent image review; one printed accent was corrected. The Holy Saturday rubrics remain a separate bounded review. A further bounded example directly compares 1606 Second Sunday and 1657 First Sunday after Pentecost: numbering and Gospel change, while the identified epistle and chant units are retained. These are descriptive incipits and appointments, not complete literal transcriptions of the propers. This supports one instance of the Monitum claim without verifying all Sundays or comparing every chant against a Roman exemplar. A separate full declared-constituent Canon comparison now supplies both source-ordered readings, including the identified seasonal forms printed within the 1606 Canon and before the 1657 main Canon. That placement difference does not establish liturgical abolition. This added comparison does not itself establish a substantive Canon revision or identify the exact native predecessor state; both Canon snapshots remain parentless and materialize their own text. The calendar comparison covers March only; other months, the rank system as a whole and the feasts' Mass formularies remain uncompared. The absence of a printed 19 March entry in 1606 is a reading of that calendar line, not proof that no Joseph Mass existed in the book or in house use.
transitions.summary: Further Romanization changes three complete Ordinary prayer units and the printed Holy Saturday ending: expanded Confiteor, replaced Orate and response, revised and relocated Suscipe Trinitas, and relocation of Spiritum nobis from a Postcommunio heading to the integrated Vespers sequence. A paired Pentecost Sunday example also changes numbering and Gospel while retaining the epistle, gradual and Alleluia. The March calendar is also recast: grades change from lessons-and-Masses notation to M./MM./Sermo, Albinus and Cuthbert disappear, and Lucius, the Forty Martyrs, Joseph, Joachim and Gabriel are printed.

The roman-1570-canon-missae reading is not a reliable basis for word comparison at several loci: it reads Et quotquot where the print has Ut quotquot, omits et before in ipso and places in ipso after the doxology rubric (the print has Per ipsum: et cum ipso: et in ipso: before bis signat inter pectus et calicem), and omits the printed Amen after the Memento of the dead. The added feasts are not named here because the Glagolitic was not transliterated; their dates match feasts added to the Roman calendar after 1631 (for example the Guardian Angels on 2 October and Didacus, Gertrude, Felix of Valois, Andrew Avellino, Elizabeth of Hungary and John of the Cross in November), but that identification is an inference from dates. transitions.limitations: Bounded to two months. The saint names were read on the images by Glagolitic letter shape and agree with feasts of the Roman calendar on those dates (John Cantius, Josaphat, Sylvester Gozzolini; Josaphat's and Sylvester's universal extensions are usually dated 1882 and 1890), but no complete transliteration was made and those extension dates were not checked in a primary act here. Other October–November rows are unchanged in occupancy (for example 3, 11, 12, 16, 22–24, 29, 30 October and 16, 27, 28 November stay empty); 1893 drops the Kalends column and the Mass page references and uses Arabic day numbers, a presentational change not counted. No claim that 1893 is the first Glagolitic book with these feasts: supplements may have carried them earlier, and the exemplar of 1893 (1741, a later supplement, or the Latin typical edition) is not established.
transitions.summary: Between the 1741 printing and 1893 the calendar gains entries on 20 October and 14 November, previously empty, and a new first-named feast on 26 November, which previously held only Peter of Alexandria.
